item.title: Detroit Red Wings play with fire, scorched by Flames in 2nd period
item.description: A couple nights after facing hardly any shots, Detroit Red Wings goalie John Gibson saw far too many in a rough second period against the Calgary Flames on Saturday, Oct. 24. Gibson surrendered three goals on 10 shots in the second, breaking a tie as the Wings fell to the Flames, 4-1, at Scotiabank Saddledome to snap a six-game point streak for Detroit (4-4-3). It was a strong contrast from his two periods of work on Thursday in Vancouver, when he faced just five shots – stopping four – in a 5-2 win over the Canucks. THROUGH 10 GAMES: Young players enthusiasm help Red Wings endure 'all the crap' The loss was the Wings’ final game at the Saddledome, which will be replaced with a new arena for the 2027-28 arena. The Wings finished their run at the Saddledome, which opened for the 1983-84 season, with a 30-33-2-2 regular-season record at the arena shaped like, well, a saddle. The loss also kept the Wings from fully joining an increasingly crowded Eastern Conference wild-card picture: at 11 points, the Wings are one point back of a block of four teams (Washington Capitals, New York Islanders, Montreal Canadiens and Florida Panthers) tied for the second and final wild-card spot. All knotted up After going into the second period trailing 1-0 on a Joel Farabee goal, the Wings evened it on a two-man hustle play from J.T. Compher and Andrew Copp, 2:22 in. Copp sent the draw from the left side dot toward the net, where Compher chased it down and tried to put a shot on net. Goalie Devin Cooley stopped that one, but Copp, trailing to the far right post, tapped it past Cooley for his second goal of the season, and his first since Oct. 15. A flurry from the Flames The tie lasted a little over six minutes before former Saginaw Spirit star Zayne Parekh scored a wrister on the power play for his first goal this season, and sixth of his career. About 9½ minutes later, Ryan Strome stretched it to a two-goal lead with a snap shot past Gibson. That was followed less than 90 seconds later by a snapper past Gibson on the power play by Matvei Gridin. Next up: Oil spoilers? The Red Wings will wrap up their four-game Western Conference road swing with a stop in Edmonton on Monday (9:30 p.m., Detroit SportsNet). The Oilers (8-2-1) enter Sunday tied for first in the Pacific Division, but they won’t be resting on their laurels after a rough game Saturday night – a 7-2 loss to the Toronto Maple Leafs. Former MVP Leon Draisaitl scored both goals for the Oilers, assisted both times by Connor McDavid. The Oilers captain is on a monster tear to open the season, as his pair of helpers brought him to an NHL-best 33 points – eight goals, 25 assists – in just 11 games; that’s an 84-game pace of 252 points, which would be 38 more than the NHL record of 215 set by Wayne Gretzky in 1985-86 (albeit in only an 82-game season). The Wings return to their non-saddle-shaped arena on Thursday as they host the Chicago Blackhawks , followed by a Halloween afternoon date with the St. Louis Blues.

item.title: Texas recovers after blowing big lead, hangs on to beat Ole Miss
item.description: Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning (16) dives into the end zone for a touchdown against Mississippi linebacker Luke Ferrelliand and Mississippi linebacker Luke Ferrelli in the first quarter at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin on Saturday Oct. 24, 2026. (Jay Janner/Austin American-Statesman) AUSTIN - After surrendering a 21-point halftime lead, 19th-ranked Texas rallied to score the go-ahead touchdown on Arch Manning's 1-yard bootleg run in the final three minutes and beat No. 7 Ole Miss 34-27 to keep its SEC championship hopes alive. The Longhorns were pushed to the limit when the Rebels scored three second-half touchdowns, including a fumble recovery in the end zone, to tie the game at 24-24 on the third play of the fourth quarter. Texas' Alex January blocked a 58-yard field goal as Ole Miss tried to cut into its seven-point deficit. Raleek Brown, who ran for 157 yards, keyed a late drive leading to a 33-yard field goal by Gianni Spetic with 2:25 to boost the lead to 10 points. The Rebels got within seven points with 1:22 left and then recovered an onside kick that the Longhorns couldn't corral. Texas survived after Jelani McDonald intercepted Trinidad Chambliss' pass in the end zone as time expired. The Longhorns improved to 5-2 overall and evened their SEC record at 2-2. Ole Miss fell to 5-2 and 3-2. All but given up for dead after losses to Oklahoma and Florida, the Longhorns came out inspired and motivated, and Manning stepped up with his best performance of the year in the first half before having three turnovers to keep Ole Miss in the game. Ole Miss' comeback to tie the game began with a sack of Manning resulting in a fumble recovery in the end zone by defensive end Kam Franklin for a touchdown. Chambliss then connected with Horatio Fields on a pair of touchdown passes of 6 and 27 yards, victimizing cornerback Kade Phillips on two perfect throws. The second score came on the third play of the fourth quarter. Texas Longhorns linebacker Rasheem Biles (3) celebrates his interception with teammates Justin Cryer (28) against Mississippi in the second quarter at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin on Saturday Oct. 24, 2026. (Jay Janner/Austin American-Statesman) The Longhorns, misfiring the entire third quarter, put together an 80-yard scoring drive to retake the lead at 31-24 with the help of a gigantic 47-yard run by Brown. Sophomore Michael Terry III, the fourth-string running back, ripped off gains of 12 and 19 yards to the lip of the goal-line before Manning scored on a perfectly timed 1-yard bootleg run. Texas jumped out to a 24-3 in the first half with three consecutive touchdown drives and a goal-line stand for its best half of the season. But the double-digit lead for the fifth game in a row should have been much bigger. Manning came out on fire. (Jay Janner/Austin American-Statesman) AUSTIN - After surrendering a 21-point halftime lead, 19th-ranked Texas rallied to score the go-ahead touchdown on Arch Manning's 1-yard bootleg run in the final three minutes and beat No. 7 Ole Miss 34-27 to keep its SEC championship hopes alive. The second score came on the third play of the fourth quarter. Texas Longhorns linebacker Rasheem Biles (3) celebrates his interception with teammates Justin Cryer (28) against Mississippi in the second quarter at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin on Saturday Oct. 24, 2026. (Jay Janner/Austin American-Statesman) The Longhorns, misfiring the entire third quarter, put together an 80-yard scoring drive to retake the lead at 31-24 with the help of a gigantic 47-yard run by Brown. Sophomore Michael Terry III, the fourth-string running back, ripped off gains of 12 and 19 yards to the lip of the goal-line before Manning scored on a perfectly timed 1-yard bootleg run. Texas jumped out to a 24-3 in the first half with three consecutive touchdown drives and a goal-line stand for its best half of the season. But the double-digit lead for the fifth game in a row should have been much bigger. Manning came out on fire. The junior quarterback completed 13 of 19 throws in the opening half with one touchdown and an interception. He should have had two scoring tosses, but Cam Coleman dropped an easy catch with nothing but green in front. Ryan Wingo did haul in a perfect pass for a 50-yard score. item.title: Raleek Brown helps No. 19 Texas Longhorns avoid a devastating loss against No. 7 Ole Miss
item.description: Texas Longhorns linebacker Rasheem Biles (3) celebrates an end zone interception with his teammates in the second quarter of the Longhorns' game against the Mississippi Rebels at Royal-Memorial Stadium in Austin, Oct. 24, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) Needing a win to keep its College Football Playoff hopes alive, the Texas Longhorns managed to secure one Saturday night. Texas held off an Ole Miss rally and avoided a complete collapse in the second half of a 34-27 win over No. 7 Ole Miss . With the win at Royal-Memorial Stadium, No. 19 Texas (5-2, 2-2) snapped a two-game losing streak. More: Subscribe to the Statesman's Texas sports newsletter Saturday's victory was also UT's second over a top-10 opponent this season. Leading the Longhorns to a victory was running back Raleek Brown, who rushed for 157 yards, and Ryan Wingo, who had 111 receiving yards. The UT defense also intercepted three passes that were thrown by Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who entered the game as a Heisman Trophy contender, with the last of those turnovers being recorded on the game's final snap. View this post on Instagram A post shared by hookem.com (@hookemdotcom) Behind Arch Manning, Texas seizes another double-digit lead After Ole Miss went 3-and-out on its first drive, the two teams traded field goals. Then things got weird. During a four-play sequence in the first quarter, the following headlines and highlights took place: Texas offensive lineman Trevor Goosby suffered an apparent leg injury and was carted off the field. Arch Manning was intercepted by Ole Miss cornerback Jalyn Crawford. Trinidad Chambliss was intercepted by UT linebacker Justin Cryer. Texas receiver Cam Coleman dropped what should have been a 59-yard touchdown. Thanks to a 2-yard touchdown run by Manning – the quarterback's first rushing score of the season – Texas exited the opening frame with a 10-3 lead. The Longhorns then returned to the end zone in the opening minutes of the second quarter during a touchdown drive that featured Manning rushing for 19 yards on a 3rd-and-17 attempt and Ryan Wingo hauling in a 50-yard toss. More: How Steve Sarkisian, Arch Manning, Texas Longhorns grade in midseason report card By the end of the first half, Texas had added sophomore running back Michael Terry III's first career touchdown run to the box score and had linebacker Rasheem Biles intercept a 4th-and-goal pass near the goal line in the waning minutes. Those two plays gave UT its largest halftime lead over a ranked opponent since the Longhorns also held a 24-3 edge halfway through their 2024 trip to Michigan. Texas Longhorns offensive lineman Trevor Goosby (74) leaves the field in a cart after going down with an injury in the first quarter of the Longhorns' game against the Mississippi Rebels at Royal-Memorial Stadium in Austin, Oct. 24, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) Needing a win to keep its College Football Playoff hopes alive, the Texas Longhorns managed to secure one Saturday night. Texas held off an Ole Miss rally and avoided a complete collapse in the second half of a 34-27 win over No. 7 Ole Miss . With the win at Royal-Memorial Stadium, No. 19 Texas (5-2, 2-2) snapped a two-game losing streak. The UT defense also intercepted three passes that were thrown by Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who entered the game as a Heisman Trophy contender, with the last of those turnovers being recorded on the game's final snap. View this post on Instagram A post shared by hookem.com (@hookemdotcom) Behind Arch Manning, Texas seizes another double-digit lead After Ole Miss went 3-and-out on its first drive, the two teams traded field goals. Then things got weird. During a four-play sequence in the first quarter, the following headlines and highlights took place: Texas offensive lineman Trevor Goosby suffered an apparent leg injury and was carted off the field. Arch Manning was intercepted by Ole Miss cornerback Jalyn Crawford. Trinidad Chambliss was intercepted by UT linebacker Justin Cryer. Texas receiver Cam Coleman dropped what should have been a 59-yard touchdown. Thanks to a 2-yard touchdown run by Manning – the quarterback's first rushing score of the season – Texas exited the opening frame with a 10-3 lead. The Longhorns then returned to the end zone in the opening minutes of the second quarter during a touchdown drive that featured Manning rushing for 19 yards on a 3rd-and-17 attempt and Ryan Wingo hauling in a 50-yard toss. More: How Steve Sarkisian, Arch Manning, Texas Longhorns grade in midseason report card By the end of the first half, Texas had added sophomore running back Michael Terry III's first career touchdown run to the box score and had linebacker Rasheem Biles intercept a 4th-and-goal pass near the goal line in the waning minutes. Those two plays gave UT its largest halftime lead over a ranked opponent since the Longhorns also held a 24-3 edge halfway through their 2024 trip to Michigan. Texas Longhorns offensive lineman Trevor Goosby (74) leaves the field in a cart after going down with an injury in the first quarter of the Longhorns' game against the Mississippi Rebels at Royal-Memorial Stadium in Austin, Oct. 24, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) Ole Miss keeps Texas on its heels, but Longhorns survive Over its past two losses against Oklahoma and Florida, Texas had built 17-7 and 17-3 leads before spoiling both double-digit advantages. So a sold-out crowd at Royal-Memorial Stadium likely didn't feel much relief at halftime despite the Longhorns' 21-point lead. And it didn't take long for the Rebels to make those fans sweat. Ole Miss took advantage of Goosby's absence as Blake Purchase blew past Andre Cojoe on the left side of UT's offensive line to sack Manning and force a fumble that the Rebels recovered for a touchdown. Chambliss then threw a 6-yard touchdown pass to make it a 24-17 game with 6:46 left in the third quarter. More: Photos from DKR as the Longhorns play the Rebels Ole Miss outscored Texas by 14 points in the third quarter and held the Longhorns to 19 yards of offense. To open the fourth quarter, Chambliss then threw a 27-yard touchdown pass to Horatio Fields to tie the game. But Texas finally found a spark on offense in the fourth quarter as Texas put together a six-play, 80-yard drive that consisted of all runs and was capped by Manning's 1-yard run on a bootleg. Although Manning got his second touchdown of the day, the biggest plays on that drive were Brown's 47-yard sprint through the Ole Miss defense and a 19-yard gain by Terry. Texas blocked an Ole Miss field goal on the following drive, and then added Gianni Spetic's 33-yard kick on the other end . The Rebels had one more rally in them, however, and Ole Miss kicked a field goal and then recovered an onside kick in the final minutes. But after Ole Miss drove to UT's 24-yard-line with nine seconds left, Chambliss threw two incomplete passes before Jelani McDonald intercepted an end-zone heave to end the game. Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning (16) huddles with his team in the second quarter of the Longhorns' game against the Mississippi Rebels at Royal-Memorial Stadium in Austin, Oct. 24, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) Longhorns to continue homestand next week against Mississippi State While attempting to build off any momentum that it seized on Saturday night, Texas will return to Royal-Memorial Stadium next weekend for its third straight home game. Mississippi State will be the Longhorns' guest on Halloween night. More: Texas coach Steve Sarkisian explains why he likes a 24-team CFP This season, Mississippi State is 4-3 with a 2-3 mark in SEC play. The Bulldogs are coming off a 23-15 loss to Oklahoma this weekend. Texas owns a 4-2 lead in an all-time series with Mississippi State that dates back to 1921. The Longhorns have beaten Mississippi State in each of the past two seasons, but Texas had to rally to an overtime win in Starkville last year . item.title: Jaylen Brown reveals there is a bit of conflict with former co-star Jayson Tatum
item.description: Jaylen Brown reveals there is a bit of conflict with former co-star Jayson Tatum originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown played alongside each other for nearly a decade on the Boston Celtics . That came to an end when the Celtics ' front office, led by Brad Stevens, decided to trade Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers . Unfortunately for the Celtics, that trade helped their rivals convince LeBron James to sign for them. A Tatum interview clip with Bleacher Report recently went viral about how he was caught off guard by the trade. Brown simply responded with a cap emoji because he believes that Tatum is not telling the truth about knowing about the trade. Jaylen Brown admits there is a bit of animosity between him and Jayson Tatum During their days together in Boston, it felt like Tatum and Brown were extremely close. They were the superstar duo of the team, and they reached two NBA Finals together, winning one of them. It was a successful partnership, but it seems that it has not gone beyond their stint in Boston. Brown seems dismissive whenever Tatum is brought up. However, he did accuse Tatum of lying about not knowing about the trade. That is mostly because everyone knows that Tatum is the superstar, and Stevens likely consulted him when the trade was coming around. MORE: Jayson Tatum breaks his silence about Jaylen Brown accusing him of lying No one in the world knows about the real situation except for Brown, Tatum, their management, and the Celtics. With this situation, it looks like Brown still has respect for Tatum, but there is some conflict between the two that everyone is noticing as well. "I didn't see the full thing, but I saw that he said it's no beef, and I think he's right... We accomplished some great things; he's a hell of a basketball player, he's got a great PR team. There's no beef, but it might be a little lamb chops and some gravy. He should stay ready at all times," Brown said after the 76ers' latest game on Saturday . While the overall message is that they are okay, there is some shade being thrown. The comment about the PR team came out of the blue, which is probably a bigger part of the dynamic than what people see. This is definitely an interesting situation because the 76ers and the Celtics will be having a lot of duels in the 2026-27 NBA season. item.title: Who plays on 'Sunday Night Football' tonight? Time, TV channel, schedule, live stream for NFL Week 7 game
item.description: Who plays on 'Sunday Night Football' tonight? Time, TV channel, schedule, live stream for NFL Week 7 game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Seattle Seahawks are facing the daunting task of defending a Super Bowl championship, and no one knows how tough that is more than the Kansas City Chiefs . On Sunday night, those two sides will meet for a rare matchup. The Seahawks are 3-3 on the year, underwhelming a bit after bulldozing the competition through the Super Bowl last year. Quarterback Sam Darnold has had turnover issues since returning from injury, but the Seahawks offense has also had issues running the ball while adjusting to a new offensive coordinator. For the Chiefs, Kansas City is undefeated on the young season, seemingly returning to its winning ways following a rough 2025. Kenneth Walker is the big story, as the Super Bowl 60 MVP returns to Seattle for the first time since signing with the Chiefs. Stopping Walker will be paramount for the Seahawks, while Walker hopes to show Seattle that the team made a mistake letting him go. Here's what's more to know about this week's "Sunday Night Football" matchup. Who plays on 'Sunday Night Football' tonight? Matchup : Seahawks vs. Chiefs Location : Lumen Field, Seattle The Seahawks will host the Chiefs in this week's "Sunday Night Football" matchup, a battle of teams that won three of the last four Super Bowls. What time is the NFL game on tonight? Date : Sunday, October 25 Time : 8:20 p.m. ET, 5:20 p.m. PT The "Sunday Night Football" game between the Seahawks and Chiefs will kick off from Lumen Field in Seattle, Washington, at 8:20 p.m. ET, 5:20 p.m. local time. What channel is 'Sunday Night Football' on? TV channel : NBC Live stream : DIRECTV | Peacock | Fubo As always, NBC will have the broadcast for "Sunday Night Football," with Mike Tirico and Cris Collinsworth on the call. Alternate streaming options include DIRECTV and Fubo, which offer free trials, along with Peacock. Sunday Night Football radio station Radio station: SiriusXM app and channels 192 (Seahawks), 193 (Chiefs) Fans can find the radio broadcast of Seahawks vs. Chiefs on the SiriusXM app, or in your vehicle on channels 192 (Seahawks broadcast) and 193 (Chiefs broadcast). The SiriusXM Sports Pass allows fans to listen to live game broadcasts of the NFL, MLB, NBA, NHL, college football and basketball, the PGA Tour, NASCAR and more. item.title: New London's Hicks edges out Colonel Crawford's Stirm in photo finish
item.description: GALION - For most runners, a photo finish is something you only see in movies. New London's Carter Hicks must be a movie star then, because this is his second such ending to a race in the last month. “More than I can count," he laughed when asked how many times this has happened before. "It was the same thing at Ontario, came down to that.” DIVISION IV GIRLS: Crestline nabs program's first district cross country title Four weeks ago at the Bill Brown Invitational he was vying for runner-up honors and ended up missing it by five-hundredths of a second. At Saturday's Division IV district meet, Hicks edged out fellow junior Isaac Stirm of Colonel Crawford by fractions of a second as both crossed the finish line in 16:22.5 — the timing software didn't go past tenths of a second. One official saw Hicks' neon green jersey cross first, another saw Stirm's black and gold. After consulting the finish line camera, they agreed Hicks won by a hair. "I knew it was going to be a close race today because Isaac had a good race last week," Hicks said. "I knew he was gonna be right on my tail the whole race ... I feed off people pushing me and close races like that for sure. “I knew I was the favorite to win today and if I came out here and executed, I could win today.” FINDLAY: 7 PRs help Lexington nab Division II district boys cross country title Stirm was hoping it would be him crossing first, though. “My goal was to win, but it’s fine because we still got next week” he said. “It pushed me a lot, he really pulled me through the race. And in my opinion, this is a pretty tough course with the hills and stuff.” Most importantly, they'll both be heading to Tiffin next weekend for the regional meet with their teammates as the photo finish also determined second and third in the team scoring — New London totaled a 94 to Colonel Crawford's 95. “It thought it would come down to us and Crestview today and it was actually really close between us and Colonel Crawford," Hicks said. "Me winning was the difference.” Seniors Ryan Twinning (8th, 17:28.8), Fritz McCully (24th), and Trace Landis (42nd) along with sophomores Luke Fawcett (28th), Logan Stanley (39th), and Michael Hardman (47th) rounded out the team placings for New London. Seniors Landon Strausbaugh (12th) and Gordie Ekin (30th), juniors Christian Mott (21st), Wyatt Burge (51st), Grayden Bohach (57th), and sophomore Bryce Parsons (36th) made up Colonel Crawford finishers. “I think the team is hyped for regionals and I’m really excited to go," Stirm said. Stirm was coming off a Northern 10 championship a week earlier and had this race planned out ahead of time to near perfection even taking the lead late down the home stretch before Hicks found a final surge at the finish line. “Isaac had a great race and that’s great to see," Colonel Crawford coach Jordan Kiess said. item.title: 'Make sure this old vintage vehicle is running well on the road': MS Dhoni shares cryptic message on his IPL future with CSK
item.description: 'Make sure this old vintage vehicle is running well on the road': MS Dhoni shares cryptic message on his IPL future with CSK originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: MS Dhoni hinted that he will decide on another IPL season before December. He missed all of IPL 2026 because of a calf problem and fitness concerns. CSK finished eighth in IPL 2026 after ending last in 2025 under Ruturaj Gaikwad. 'Decision before December': MS Dhoni breaks silence on CSK future & retirement timeline MS Dhoni described himself as an old vintage vehicle that needs to keep running smoothly on the road while talking about his Indian Premier League future. The former India captain suggested a final decision on whether he plays one more season could come before December, though he stopped well short of a clear answer. The World Cup-winning former India captain was speaking at a healthcare event in Bengaluru on Saturday, where he was asked whether he would like to have another go at the IPL. He missed the whole of IPL 2026 because of fitness issues, mainly linked to his calf, so the question was significant. MORE: Ayush Mhatre injury update: CSK youngster out for four months after surgery He first turned to the doctor on stage and made it clear that his body would have to clear a proper check before anything is decided. “Doc, I will have to go through the test. You will have to give me the report, and then before December, I will have to see, you know, how strong I am to maybe play one more season," he said. The wicketkeeper-batter then moved to a second scenario, in which he isn’t strong enough to carry on. In typical Dhoni fashion, he put the responsibility on the people looking after his health, and he compared himself to a machine that requires careful maintenance. He added: “And if I am not, then, you know, you will have to make sure that you do everything right with me and make sure that this old vintage vehicle is running well on the road. So all the pressure is on them.” #WATCH | Bengaluru, Karnataka | On his IPL future, Former Indian Cricket Team Captain Mahendra Singh Dhoni says, "I'll have to go through the tests. You'll have to give me the report, and before December, I'll need to assess how strong I am and whether I can play one more season. If I'm not fit enough, then you'll have to make sure you do everything right to get this old vintage vehicle running smoothly on the road..." (24.10) — ANI (@ANI) October 24, 2026 MS Dhoni's diminishing influence on CSK Dhoni’s place in the CSK batting order has diminished over the last two years. He now walks in during the slog overs, with the task of lifting the total and showing fans a glimpse of the trademark power-hitting that made him famous. However, the team’s results have slipped since Ruturaj Gaikwad took over the captaincy in 2024. CSK ended at the bottom of the table in IPL 2025, and they improved only slightly in IPL 2026 by finishing eighth.

(24.10) — ANI (@ANI) October 24, 2026 MS Dhoni's diminishing influence on CSK Dhoni’s place in the CSK batting order has diminished over the last two years. He now walks in during the slog overs, with the task of lifting the total and showing fans a glimpse of the trademark power-hitting that made him famous. However, the team’s results have slipped since Ruturaj Gaikwad took over the captaincy in 2024. CSK ended at the bottom of the table in IPL 2025, and they improved only slightly in IPL 2026 by finishing eighth. Their last IPL title came in 2023, when Dhoni was still leading the side, which is a reminder of how much has changed in a short time. MORE: Not CSK: Ashwin reveals Pandya's next IPL franchise Dhoni’s decision matters for CSK far beyond one more season Dhoni’s remarks were funny, but they also revealed a lot about where CSK stand right now. The franchise has been built around his presence for so long that any talk of another season sends a ripple through the fan base, and his call before December will shape how the team plans for the next mini-auction and beyond. A side that has finished at the bottom and then eighth in successive years can’t afford to drift while waiting for an answer. There is a fair argument that Dhoni’s final-overs role still has value, given his numbers and the way he is greeted at every ground. However, it is hard to ignore that a missed season and a stubborn calf injury raise doubts about how much he can still give. MORE: 'MS (Dhoni) has been a great force': Zaheer reveals how he became CSK head coach Supporters would probably prefer to see him leave on his own terms rather than push through another year of struggle. Whichever way he goes, CSK need a clear plan under Gaikwad that does not rely on one man’s decision. The captain has had two difficult seasons, and the team’s identity has to grow beyond the legend who built it. If Dhoni returns, he should do so fully fit and with a defined purpose. If he doesn’t, the club must be ready to turn the page with confidence. item.title: Caleb Wilson enters in Michael Jordan territory after first 3 NBA games
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Caleb Wilson enters in Michael Jordan territory after first 3 NBA games appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Chicago Bulls took on the Washington Wizards in their home opener on Saturday. Although Caleb Wilson soared, finishing with a double-double of 30 points and 14 rebounds, the Bulls lost 124-120. However, Wilson showed signs that he indeed can meet or even exceed expectations. Over the course of the first three games, Wilson put up points that put him in the same category as Michael Jordan , no kidding, per Novig. Wilson is now second in points scored through the first three games for a new player with 67. Jordan is first with 74. 🚨 CHICAGO BULLS HISTORY Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Caleb Wilson has scored 67 points through his first three NBA games, the SECOND-MOST by any player in Bulls history. The only player ahead of him? Michael Jordan with 74. https://t.co/w9A6jmvXOe pic.twitter.com/458LhF2UxP — Novig (@Novig) October 25, 2026 Wilson also matched Jordan’s numbers in his first two NBA games. Both scored 16 points in their first game and 21 in their second. At this point, it could be tantalizing to put Wilson in the same category as Jordan, even though he is just getting started and Jordan’s legacy needs no explanation. Still, some similarities are worth noting. For instance, Wilson and Jordan hail out of North Carolina . Both were sensations at Chapel Hill. Jordan was the National Player of the Year in 1984. Meanwhile, Wilson was a second-team All-American in his one year at North Carolina. Moreover, the Bulls drafted Jordan in 1984 with the No. 3 pick in one of the most consequential drafts in NBA history. Fast forward to 2026, and Wilson was selected No. 4 among one of the best draft classes in recent memory. When Jordan was drafted, he was the solo star for a poor team. Wilson is seen as the savior for a team that has endured years of repeated stagnation. The Bulls will play the Boston Celtics on Monday, October 26, in Boston. Related: Caleb Wilson, Matas Buzelis get fans hyped up with back-to-back dunks against Wizards Related: Bulls executive praises Caleb Wilson ‘genuine’ desire to grow after strong NBA debut

item.title: Virginia Tech Hokies Defeat Clemson in a Close Defensive Brawl: 20-16
item.description: CLEMSON, SOUTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 24: Ashton Hampton #2 of the Clemson Tigers tackles Luke Reynolds #85 of the Virginia Tech Hokies during the first quarter at Memorial Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Clemson, South Carolina. (Photo by Katie DeVaney/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Hokies had much going against them in this one, but the defense played as tough as Clemson’s. The key being that final series for Clemson with the clock running out. We know the Hokies’ bugaboos continue to plague them; dealing with running QBs, offensive line issues, and third quarter fades. This time though, Virginia Tech managed -4 stop after stop, and rallied up on offense to drive down the field and score in the air. The Program called this the play of the game, and it was… DEFENSE CALLED GAME 😤 #LetsGoHokies pic.twitter.com/JnLdnewnq5 — Virginia Tech Football (@HokiesFB) October 25, 2026 It was an Old Fashioned “Caveman Football” Effort The Hokies once again defied the rules of probability and lost the coin toss. It’s getting to be something that isn’t really even worth it. The offense went much of nowhere, and the defense returned the favor for the Tigers. The score was knotted at 0-0 for three-quarters of the 1st period until Dabo decided to gamble on his side of the 50. Clemson went for it on 4th and short. Tech’s defense had the range and the TFL to force the turnover on downs, but Tech’s offense really didn’t do a whole lot with the ball, either. That problem getting the ball across the goal line when in the red zone was an issue for both teams for this contest. John Love was gold for the game, and his first field goal (37 yards) was also the first and last score of the first quarter. With the ice broken, Clemson found some success and drove the ball down into the Hokies’ danger zone. The Tech defense managed a -4 stop as Clemson’s very capable place kicker split the uprights from 34 yards out. The Hokies tried a little “trickeration” on 4th down and they faked a punt, but the pattern was too far short of the sticks and Tech turned the ball over on downs inside their territory. The Hokie defense stepped up again, and not only stopped the Tigers, but managed to knock them out of field goal range. The ensuing Tech drive, presumably off the momentum of the stop, went all the way into the endzone for a nifty Ethan Grunkemeyer to Luke Reynolds touchdown. Too smooth 😮‍💨 #LetsGoHokies | 📺 @espn https://t.co/1t3PrrEyTU pic.twitter.com/uKE9ZRFRPx — Virginia Tech Football (@HokiesFB) October 25, 2026 Suddenly, close to the end of the half, the Hokies found themselves needing a stop and ahead 10-3. That doesn’t sound great but given the tone and tempo of this game a touchdown lead was a serious hurtle to overcome for the Clemson offense. After a convincing stop, and a Clemson punt the Hokies let the clock run out on the 3 or so seconds remaining before the half. Both teams went into their respective team rooms to go over what they thought worked and didn’t. Hokie Nation

(Photo by Katie DeVaney/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Hokies had much going against them in this one, but the defense played as tough as Clemson’s. The key being that final series for Clemson with the clock running out. We know the Hokies’ bugaboos continue to plague them; dealing with running QBs, offensive line issues, and third quarter fades. The Program called this the play of the game, and it was… DEFENSE CALLED GAME 😤 #LetsGoHokies pic.twitter.com/JnLdnewnq5 — Virginia Tech Football (@HokiesFB) October 25, 2026 It was an Old Fashioned “Caveman Football” Effort The Hokies once again defied the rules of probability and lost the coin toss. It’s getting to be something that isn’t really even worth it. The offense went much of nowhere, and the defense returned the favor for the Tigers. That problem getting the ball across the goal line when in the red zone was an issue for both teams for this contest. John Love was gold for the game, and his first field goal (37 yards) was also the first and last score of the first quarter. With the ice broken, Clemson found some success and drove the ball down into the Hokies’ danger zone. The Tech defense managed a -4 stop as Clemson’s very capable place kicker split the uprights from 34 yards out. The Hokies tried a little “trickeration” on 4th down and they faked a punt, but the pattern was too far short of the sticks and Tech turned the ball over on downs inside their territory. The Hokie defense stepped up again, and not only stopped the Tigers, but managed to knock them out of field goal range. The ensuing Tech drive, presumably off the momentum of the stop, went all the way into the endzone for a nifty Ethan Grunkemeyer to Luke Reynolds touchdown. Too smooth 😮‍💨 #LetsGoHokies | 📺 @espn https://t.co/1t3PrrEyTU pic.twitter.com/uKE9ZRFRPx — Virginia Tech Football (@HokiesFB) October 25, 2026 Suddenly, close to the end of the half, the Hokies found themselves needing a stop and ahead 10-3. That doesn’t sound great but given the tone and tempo of this game a touchdown lead was a serious hurtle to overcome for the Clemson offense. After a convincing stop, and a Clemson punt the Hokies let the clock run out on the 3 or so seconds remaining before the half. Both teams went into their respective team rooms to go over what they thought worked and didn’t. Hokie Nation worried because as we have seen all season, Tech has a “no good very bad thing” going with the third quarter. The Third Quarter Fade If it wasn’t something that you could just set a timer to, it’s certainly something that some betting house is going to offer odds on whether or not Virginia Tech manages not to do it. The 3rd quarter heartburn was in serious need of some powerful antacids for this one. The first drive for Clemson, out of the break, set the Hokies back on their heels. Clemson’s surprisingly good freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds managed to push pull prod, run, and pass in modest chunks to get the Tigers into field goal range before the Hokie defense finally caught and stopped them. The Tiger 49-yard field goal didn’t put them ahead, but it did make the score a more manageable 10-6. The Hokies, however, went 3 and out while going negative 9 yards on their next series. The OC either didn’t make major adjustments to his game plan, or he figured that the Tigers weren’t going to rush with overwhelming force. They did, and the slow developing plays that were called were just not up to defeating the very capable Clemson defensive line. Grunkemeyer was ultimately sacked 6 times in the game. Tech returned many of those favors on their QB, but neither offensive line was dominating the LOS. Eventually Clemson drove the ball down the field as the Hokie defense sort of lost focus when the Tigers used the QB power to first get Tait Reynolds to move the ball 11 yards, and then repeat the same basic play to score after doing a very credible job getting passes off to his receivers. Reynolds scored the Tigers’ only touchdown from 16 yards out. That put Clemson ahead by 3 points, 10-3, but it also woke up the Virginia Tech defense. Tech’s offense was still in a no-go zone, and the defense had to pull off a bend but don’t break for a -4 with 3:48 left in the 3rd. The Hokies managed to return the favor on the ensuing kickoff, it was another -4 for Tech, but on the drive, they had managed to get the ball out faster, and Grunkemeyer’s 27-yard strike to Que’Sean Brown might have proven something to Coaches Howle and Franklin. Quick passing plays were working under the zone and in the seams. That fact might have saved the Hokies as the game drew to a close. Nailed it, @johnlove97 🎯 #LetsGoHokies | 📺 @espn pic.twitter.com/IHbExpZSJ1 — Virginia Tech Football (@HokiesFB) October 25, 2026 The Game Came Down to the 4th A 16-13 game is not in the bag, unless the final whistle goes off. The problem was that Virginia Tech needed a touchdown to win, and a field goal to tie. There was a little birdie that told me Coach Franklin, known as a bit of a gambler, wasn’t too interested in a tie and a trudge into overtime with the rules favoring no one since both offenses were struggling in the red zone. Between the Love field goal at 12:00 on the 4th quarter clock, and the end of the game, the Hokies had to keep the Tigers from scoring anything. A field goal would make it difficult, and a touchdown would pretty much end the game. The Hokie defense managed a stop after 5 plays. Things started off pretty well with the Tigers eating up 18 quick yards, only to have the defensive line get enough pressure on Tait Reynolds that their 3rd and long attempt failed with a 3-yard loss. Que’Sean Brown put up a nice 15-yard return on the Clemson punt, but the Hokies had a holding penalty and two incomplete passes that made a nice 10-yarder to Q. Brown a big nothing. The Totten punt put the Tigers all the way back to their 7 yard line which forced the Tigers to try to run it out and they failed to get a 1st down. 4:48 The Hokies got the ball back with just short of 7 minutes on the clock. There were two issues there. First, the team needed that TD to win, but burn enough time off the clock, and get it close enough that in an emergency John Love’s foot could tie it up without giving Clemson any chances. Tech’s final drive was interesting because Howle seemed to completely abandon the idea of a 4-minute offense, and went straight to what looked like a classic 2-minute drill. They were successful enough that Clemson’s secondary began to get nervous and make mistakes. Both sides were probably pretty keyed up, because Tech made a few buffaloes too. They started off with a false start which put them five yards behind the sticks. Grunk had to scramble for 2 yards (it might have been a designed run, but at that point Tech wasn’t running so it’s safe to guess it was a scramble). Then Grunkemeyer began to get some success. A quick shovel pass tunnel screen to Reynolds got 8, Grunk hit Fatrat Brown who got beyond the sticks and pulled off a pro sideline catch for the 1st down. That loosened up the defense a bit for Jeffery Overton to grab five yards and take a little time off the clock. Then Grunkemeyer hit Tyseer Denmark for first down. item.title: What LSU Tigers coach Lane Kiffin called ‘abnormal’ after win over Auburn Tigers
item.description: Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin addressed one of the biggest factors in the program’s 2026 CFB season after a 38-17 win over the Auburn Tigers. The Tigers fell behind the competitive pack early in the 2026 CFB season with losses to Ole Miss and Kentucky in the first five weeks, which has dented their hopes of reaching the College Football Playoffs. After LSU picked up a 38-17 win over Auburn on October 24, Coach Kiffin made it a point to remind everyone about the real circumstances that have defined LSU’s start to the season. Lane Kiffin thinks LSU Tigers’ 2026 season has been abnormal Kiffin spoke to the media after the win over Auburn and was asked about the best games that LSU have played this season, ending it with an admission that LSU’s injury situation and their results are abnormal. “We’ve played really good games this year. The opening game, it was about as well as you could have played… Last week, they didn’t score against us. We’ve played really well. We’ve had five games where our backups are in at the end of the game, including 3 SEC games. That’s very abnormal.” These comments come a week after Kiffin explosively told Mississippi State to stop complaining about losing key players to injury, because LSU and other top teams have also lost players to injury already. The Tigers have lost LB Whit Weeks, Safety Dashawn Spears, WR Phillip Wright III, and are expected to be without key contributors like Charles Ross II and DT Richard Anderson. Thankfully, LSU did see TE Trey’Dez Green return to the field against Auburn, while WR Jackson Harris avoided major injury. DE Princewill Umanmielen is expected to return soon as well. QB Sam Leavitt is playing through a hamstring injury as well, so Kiffin is fair to hold the opinion he does about the team’s injury crisis being abnormal, especially with their recent results. If the Tigers manage to go the rest of the season without a loss, they will presumably be locked into the CFP. Even one more loss makes their qualifying situation dicey, so LSU and Kiffin will hope they can push through their injury crisis and continue extracting results on the field. Smith worried by what he’s seen from Arch Manning ‘Tears in my eyes’ – Dave Portnoy mocks Michigan State’s failed attempt to sabotage Nick Saban ‘Still shut you out’ – Lane Kiffin sends another shot at Mississippi State HC for injury complaints

item.title: ‘If we don’t…’ – What Lane Kiffin told LSU QB Sam Leavitt that led to dominant victory against Auburn
item.description: Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Lane Kiffin knew exactly what quarterback Sam Leavitt needed to do for the LSU Tigers to get their latest win, and he shared it after they beat Auburn. LSU finally put together the kind of offensive performance Lane Kiffin has likely been looking for, beating Auburn 38-17. Sam Leavitt led the way with four total touchdowns and 387 passing yards, as the Tigers took a 31-10 lead into halftime and never looked back. Wide receiver Jackson Harris had himself a game, finishing with 178 receiving yards and two touchdowns. It was a comfortable victory from the jump, and one that Lane Kiffin knew exactly what his quarterback had to do to achieve. Lane Kiffin reveals his ‘take care of the ball’ advice to quarterback Sam Leavitt which led to the win Turning the ball over has been one of Leavitt’s biggest issues this season. He has already thrown eight interceptions this year, which has been a big problem for LSU. The team could have boasted an even better record than their current 6-2 showing. Kiffin spoke after the game about how that needed to be addressed to secure the win against Auburn. He revealed exactly what he told his quarterback. “I just told him that this was a game, you guys heard me say before, when I feel a game early that, ‘OK, we’re really going to dominate this game if we don’t screw up,’ I say that a lot to the players and to the quarterback especially,” Kiffin said. “‘OK, hey, this is going to be a take-care-of-the-ball game,’ because we’re playing really well on the other side and we’ve got really good matchups. So he really played really well.” Leavitt had no turnovers against Auburn, which made a world of difference for the team. If he can continue to play like this, then Kiffin and the Tigers might just end up surprising some people this season. Smith worried by what he’s seen from Arch Manning ‘Tears in my eyes’ – Dave Portnoy mocks Michigan State’s failed attempt to sabotage Nick Saban

item.title: Brewers erase four-run deficit, take 2-0 World Series lead
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WI - OCTOBER 24: Sal Frelick #10 of the Milwaukee Brewers rounds the bases after hitting a solo home run in the sixth inning during Game Two of the 2026 World Series presented by Capital One between the Tampa Bay Rays and the Milwaukee Brewers at American Family Field on Saturday, October 24, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Daniel Shirey/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The 2026 Milwaukee Brewers might have to borrow a 40-year-old slogan from the Goonies: “Never Say Die.“ Tonight, the Brewers were facing Drew Rasmussen, the Tampa Bay ace and the best starting pitcher of the postseason so far. Logan Henderson, who hasn’t been at his best this postseason, suffered through a disastrous first inning. But if there was one thing that the Brewers proved against the Dodgers in the National League Championship Series, it was that no lead is safe, and this remarkable team will not ever give up. In the parlance of one of the Brewer standouts this evening, the Brewers dragged Rasmussen. The ground out at-bats. They chipped away. Peck, peck, peck. And before it was over, Milwaukee had a couple of new offensive heroes, another huge comeback win, and a 2-0 series lead. But before all that, it was a nightmare start for the Brewers. The first batter of the game, Yandy Díaz, worked for seven pitches. The last one, a changeup way below the zone, was hit weakly to shortstop. Cooper Pratt fielded it but rushed the throw, which got by Jake Bauers and into the dugout, putting Díaz at second base. An ominous omen. Henderson recovered momentarily and struck out Jonathan Aranda for the first out. But Chandler Simpson did Chandler Simpson things, knocking an RBI single into center field, after which he stole second and then scored when Junior Caminero followed with another RBI single. Henderson did retire the next two, but the Brewers would have to dig themselves out of a deep hole on this night. item.content:encoded: MILWAUKEE, WI - OCTOBER 24: Sal Frelick #10 of the Milwaukee Brewers rounds the bases after hitting a solo home run in the sixth inning during Game Two of the 2026 World Series presented by Capital One between the Tampa Bay Rays and the Milwaukee Brewers at American Family Field on Saturday, October 24, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Daniel Shirey/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The 2026 Milwaukee Brewers might have to borrow a 40-year-old slogan from the Goonies: “Never Say Die.“ Tonight, the Brewers were facing Drew Rasmussen, the Tampa Bay ace and the best starting pitcher of the postseason so far. Logan Henderson, who hasn’t been at his best this postseason, suffered through a disastrous first inning. But Chandler Simpson did Chandler Simpson things, knocking an RBI single into center field, after which he stole second and then scored when Junior Caminero followed with another RBI single. The Rays weren’t finished, though: Liam Hicks got an 0-1 cutter right down the middle and hit it out to right center, the first homer of the series, which made it 4-0 Rays with only one out on the board. Henderson did retire the next two, but the Brewers would have to dig themselves out of a deep hole on this night. Fortunately, they’re a team that has proved time and time again that they’re a team that brought their shovels to the postseason. They got to work on Rasmussen immediately in the bottom of the first: Jackson Chourio singled, moved to third on a single by Bauers, and then scored when, after a Christian Yelich strikeout, William Contreras came through as he has so many times over the past month with an RBI single through the right side of the infield. Wild Bill gets one back pic.twitter.com/gSbFvQG2h2 — Milwaukee Brewers (@Brewers) October 25, 2026 Brice Turang hit into a hard-luck second out when he hit a 109 mph line drive right at Richie Palacios. But Garrett Mitchell kept the pressure on the Rays, and hit a 112 mph single into right that scored Bauers. Pratt struck out to end the inning, but Milwaukee had immediately halved the Rays lead. G is so clutch pic.twitter.com/OPaAX0vS27 — Milwaukee Brewers (@Brewers) October 25, 2026 A leadoff walk to Victor Mesa Jr. in the second had Henderson on the precipice, but he showed some fight; Taylor Walls bunted, Mesa Jr. over to second but made the first out, and Henderson struck out Díaz and Aranda to get through the inning unscathed. Rasmussen was on his way to a quick inning in the bottom of the second, but Chourio took a hammer to his pitch count when, with two outs, he battled for 11 pitches before hitting a 105 mph groundout. It was a 1-2-3 inning for the Tampa Bay ace, but he had to work hard for it. Henderson got one more inning and made the most of it, retiring Simpson, Caminero, and Hicks in order. The Brewers were unable to score in the bottom of the inning despite Contreras’s second hit of the game (which pushed his batting average in the postseason over .400). In the top of the fourth, JoJo Romero replaced Henderson and worked around a one-out single to put up another zero. The Brewers were back on Rasmussen in the bottom of the fourth. With one out, Pratt drew a walk, and two pitches later, Sal Frelick lined a solid single into right, putting runners on the corners. David Hamilton, in a possible squeeze situation, eschewed the bunt and swung away, ultimately hitting what should’ve been a routine grounder to first. But Aranda, possibly with an eye on trying to get Pratt at home, booted it, and everyone was safe. The lead was down to one. WHAT IN THE WORLD pic.twitter.com/zNHa7J7fK3 — Milwaukee Brewers (@Brewers) October 25, 2026 The Rays worked out of the inning, but after a Chourio groundout, Rasmussen walked Bauers, which ended his evening. He was replaced by the Rays’ best lefty, Cam Booser, who faced Yelich; another manager may have gone to Andrew Vaughn as a pinch-hitter with the bases full and two out, but Pat Murphy rode with Yelich, who anticlimactically grounded out to second. The Brewer pitcher in the fifth was Dustin May. With one out, Aranda lined a double into the right-field corner, but May was able to work out of it—Aranda moved to third on a Simpson groundout, but a Pratt made an assured play on a slow Caminero chopper to end the inning and strand the Ray first baseman at third. Booser worked through the middle of the Brewers’ order in the bottom of the fifth, allowing only a walk to Turang. DL Hall replaced May in the sixth and put himself in a hole when he hit the leadoff batter, Hicks, on the right forearm. He moved over on a sacrifice by Palacios, but Hall got the second out on a strikeout of Johnny DeLuca. Mesa Jr., though, came through with a two-out single to left, but Rays third base coach Brady Williams got extremely aggressive by sending his leadfooted catcher on a single to shallow left; Chourio’s throw was on target, and Hicks was toast at home plate. CHOURIO CUTS A MAN DOWN AT THE PLATE pic.twitter.com/jlNgvVOhne — Milwaukee Brewers (@Brewers) October 25, 2026 The Brewers seized the momentum from getting the final out at home. With lefty Ian Seymor on to face the bottom of the Brewer order, Frelick, of all people, battled for nine pitches, and on the last one he took a 93 mph fastball right over the heart of the plate and hit it out to center field. Tie ballgame. SAL FRELICK WITH THE BIGGEST SWING OF HIS LIFE pic.twitter.com/XpoY5dfa3M — Milwaukee Brewers (@Brewers) October 25, 2026 Milwaukee kept making Seymour work hard. Hamilton fell into a 1-2 count but hit seven foul balls before striking out. Chourio saw eight pitches before he struck out. With two outs, Bauers worked a walk. Yelich, against another lefty, hit a pop-up to shallow left, but it was sort of in no-man’s land between Walls, the shortstop, and Simpson, the left fielder. Some indecision about whose ball it was led to Simpson fielding it awkwardly; he had it in his glove, but he fell down while making the catch and when the glove hit the ground, the ball popped out. Bauers made it to third, while Yelich had a “single.” With runners on the corners and two out, the Rays needed to pull Seymour, who had thrown 34 pitches and not recored an out. Kevin Cash went to righty Tyler Wells to face Contreras, who was definitely the batter the Brewers wanted up in this situation. The move to Wells worked, though; Contreras grounded out to third to end the inning. Still, for the second time in three games, the Brewers had erased an early 4-0 deficit by the end of the sixth inning. With the game tied, the Brewers pivoted firmly toward their “A” bullpen, as Abner Uribe entered the game in place of Hall, facing Walls and then, for the second time in two days, the top of the Tampa Bay order. Troublingly, Uribe walked Walls, the worst hitter on the Rays’ roster, to set up the top of the order. Uribe got ahead of Díaz, and the Tampa Bay DH fouled off a bunch of pitches to stay alive, but Uribe finally got him with a slider for the first out. Aranda, who singled off of Uribe on Friday night,

item.title: Sharks Locker Room: San Jose Had Winning Road Trip, But It Didn’t Feel That Way Tonight
item.description: BOSTON — The San Jose Sharks echoed the same theme, after a 6-4 loss to the Boston Bruins. “Be better in front of the net,” Will Smith said of four of the Bruins goals, which happened right in front of goalie Alex Nedeljkovic . “They’re very preventable.” Smith wasn’t a pointing a finger at just his defensemen, but at the whole team, including himself. “We got to help Ned out,” Smith said. Michael Misa , Kiefer Sherwood , Dmitry Orlov , and Smith scored in the back-and-forth tilt. In the end, the Sharks came out of a six-game road trip with a 3-2-1 record, but it feels like it could’ve been more, after a 3-1 third period lead at Detroit turned into an OT loss and tonight’s 3-2 third period edge ended in a regulation defeat. After the game, Smith praised Jeremy Swayman’s play, Nedeljkovic shared the key on how the San Jose Sharks can defend harder, Orlov discussed the expectations for this team, and Warsofsky summarized where the squad is at 12 games into the season. A deeper game story with micro-stats from Stathletes and game action clips, Sharks Insight, will be published soon. Will Smith Smith, on Swayman's save on him, Bruins up 5-4 late in 3rd: "I think I honestly had that one. It was a quick pump fake and backhander. He made a hell of a save, so we got to tip your cap. He's a hell of a goalie and he played good tonight." — Sheng Peng (@Sheng_Peng) October 25, 2026 Alex Nedeljkovic Nedeljkovic, on all the net front goals that Boston scored: I think that’s where they scored all their goals except for the Pasta one. All that is, just outwilling guys and wanting to defend harder than the other team wants to score. All it comes down to, no X’s and O’s, and we had bodies in the area, I think, on all of them, it’s just outwilling them a little bit more, just being a little harder on our sticks. I can do a better job, maybe swallowing up another puck or two there and killing plays or putting rebounds in better spots as well. Dmitry Orlov Orlov: "On paper, everybody expects us to be a good team. But right now, we have to prove it. Not just be a good team on paper. We have to show up every game and battle." — Sheng Peng (@Sheng_Peng) October 25, 2026 Orlov, on the San Jose Sharks losing net front battles: We just shoot ourselves in the foot again. It kind of happens almost every game. We [don’t] battle, [don’t] win the battles when we have to. We not playing more hungry, for the battles, for the puck, and lost focus sometimes. It’s why we give up some goals. Ryan Warsofsky Warsofsky, on the Michael Misa pass to Ty Dellandrea that led to the David Pastrnak goal: We make a play on the entry, where we got to be smarter than that. We try to make a cross-ice pass with four seconds left in the power play. Pastrnak comes out of the box, he scores. So we got to be smarter. Warsofsky, on the 3-2-1 road trip: We got some results. item.title: Wisconsin makes noise with upset win over USC
item.description: Anthony Wahl-Imagn Images Wisconsin makes noise with upset win over USC appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Wisconsin football once faced hot seat concerns for head coach Luke Fickell . Now the Badgers coach helped put USC coach Lincoln Riley there. All thanks to Wisconsin trouncing the No. 16 Trojans 24-7 in Madison Saturday. The fans flooded the field at Madison after watching their team pull off the latest top 25 upset on a wild Oct. 24. THE SCENE IN MADISON 😮 pic.twitter.com/1sklp5an4Y Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — ESPN College Football (@ESPNCFB) October 25, 2026 USC joined No. 2 BYU, No. 8 Texas Tech, No. 11 Tennessee and No. 15 Iowa in losing during the same weekend. But Wisconsin delivered its first statement win in the era of Fickell. The former Cincinnati coach once came in decorated with a past College Football Playoff resume. He even left the Bearcats during a time they transitioned to the Big 12 Conference. But now Fickell pulled off an epic masterclass of coaching by pivoting back to past Badgers tactics. Wisconsin battered USC with its ground game, tallying 142 rushing yards there. The Badgers then delivered five sacks of USC quarterback Jayden Maiava , including intercepting him twice. Wisconsin turned to defense, ball control and owning the line of scrimmage to pull off this upset. These tactics turned the Badgers into a Rose Bowl and Cotton Bowl contender under past coaches Barry Alvarez, Bret Bielema, then Paul Chryst. So the Badgers now will more than likely garner top 25 attention. Meanwhile, USC legend Keyshawn Johnson called out Riley following the rough loss , saying “it ain’t working out” and “tough decisions must be made.” USC’s remaining schedule doesn’t lighten either. The Trojans face three teams ranked in the top 10 (Ohio State, Indiana and UCLA) still. Related: Why Virginia Tech HC James Franklin didn’t go for the tie vs. Clemson down 16-13 Related: Luke Fickell’s ‘gritty ain’t pretty’ declaration will have Wisconsin fans hyped

THE SCENE IN MADISON 😮 pic.twitter.com/1sklp5an4Y Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — ESPN College Football (@ESPNCFB) October 25, 2026 USC joined No. 2 BYU, No. 8 Texas Tech, No. 11 Tennessee and No. 15 Iowa in losing during the same weekend. But Wisconsin delivered its first statement win in the era of Fickell. The former Cincinnati coach once came in decorated with a past College Football Playoff resume. He even left the Bearcats during a time they transitioned to the Big 12 Conference. But now Fickell pulled off an epic masterclass of coaching by pivoting back to past Badgers tactics. Wisconsin battered USC with its ground game, tallying 142 rushing yards there. The Badgers then delivered five sacks of USC quarterback Jayden Maiava , including intercepting him twice. Wisconsin turned to defense, ball control and owning the line of scrimmage to pull off this upset. These tactics turned the Badgers into a Rose Bowl and Cotton Bowl contender under past coaches Barry Alvarez, Bret Bielema, then Paul Chryst. So the Badgers now will more than likely garner top 25 attention. Meanwhile, USC legend Keyshawn Johnson called out Riley following the rough loss , saying “it ain’t working out” and “tough decisions must be made.” USC’s remaining schedule doesn’t lighten either. The Trojans face three teams ranked in the top 10 (Ohio State, Indiana and UCLA) still. Related: Why Virginia Tech HC James Franklin didn’t go for the tie vs. Clemson down 16-13 Related: Luke Fickell’s ‘gritty ain’t pretty’ declaration will have Wisconsin fans hyped

item.title: ‘Disappointed!’- Kalen DeBoer calls out Alabama’s biggest problem after Texas A&M win
item.description: Photo by Jason Clark/Getty Images Kalen DeBoer has made his frustration with Alabama’s running game clear despite the Crimson Tide securing a much-needed victory over Texas A&M. Alabama entered the matchup following consecutive SEC defeats to Georgia and Tennessee, leaving DeBoer under pressure to get his team back on track. The win provides some relief, but the head coach knows his side must improve offensively before the final stretch of the regular season. Kalen DeBoer demands more from Alabama Crimson Tide’s struggling run game Speaking after the victory , DeBoer praised Alabama’s determination to fight for four quarters but was far less pleased with the team’s ground attack. When asked about the running game, the Crimson Tide head coach did not hide his disappointment. “Disappointed, disappointed,” DeBoer said. “The stats, that’s all you gotta really look at, and we needed more out of that run game to open up some things for us.” DeBoer also highlighted missed blocks, negative rushing plays and defenders getting through the line as areas that need to be addressed. “When we get some negative yards and have guys that are unblocked at the point of attack, or falling off blocks, those are things that we gotta get back to the basics, and we gotta get better at.” The concern is particularly relevant with young quarterback Keelon Russell leading the offence. Alabama needs a more consistent rushing threat to help create opportunities and take pressure off its passing game. Russell did, however, earn praise for his response after some early struggles, with DeBoer highlighting several important throws late in the contest. Wide receiver Rico Scott also impressed, making key contributions when Alabama needed someone to step up. The Crimson Tide now have a bye week before returning to SEC action against LSU, giving the coaching staff time to work on the issues exposed against Texas A&M. However, Alabama will also have to monitor injuries. Offensive lineman William Sanders suffered a lower-extremity injury and could miss several weeks. The victory offers DeBoer some breathing room, but Alabama’s next challenge is turning its late-game resilience into a more complete performance. Improving the run game will be a key part of that task. Read more: ‘You should be panicked’ – Stephen A. Smith worried by what he’s seen from Arch Manning ‘Tears in my eyes’ – Dave Portnoy mocks Michigan State’s failed attempt to sabotage Nick Saban ‘Still shut you out’ – Lane Kiffin sends another shot at Mississippi State HC for injury complaints

item.title: O'Shaquie Foster Put On The Performance Of A Lifetime — Now History Is 1 Fight Away
item.description: NEWARK, NEW JERSEY - JULY 06: Detail of a blood drop beneath the eye of O'Shaquie Foster as he trades punches with Robson Conceicao of Brazil during their WBC Jr. Lightweight World Title fight at Prudential Center on July 06, 2024 in Newark, New Jersey. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) Getty Images O’Shaquie Foster just put on a masterful display of boxing at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas. He dropped Emanuel Navarrete twice in the 12th round en route to a dominant unanimous-decision victory (118-108x2, 115-111). On paper, this fight looked like it had a chance to be the Fight of the Year. Instead, it turned out to be one of the best in-ring performances in 2026 by a single fighter. Now, Foster is one fight away from becoming the undisputed champion at 130 pounds — which is something that has never been done in boxing. Foster simply picked Navarrete apart. He exposed the Mexican’s sloppy feet and slow hands and he did it fighting primarily in the pocket. Here is a look at some of his handiwork. Navarrete vs. Foster Key Facts Detail Info Result O’Shaquie Foster def. Emanuel Navarrete, unanimous decision Scorecards 118-108, 115-111, 118-108 Knockdowns Two, both by Foster in Round 12 Titles Foster retained the WBC title and won the IBF and WBO titles Date Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026 Venue Frost Bank Center, San Antonio, Texas Broadcast DAZN Records Foster 26-3 (12 KOs), Navarrete 40-3-1 (33 KOs) How Did Fighters React to O’Shaquie Foster’s Win? Fighters throughout the sport took to X with reactions. Foster even got acknowledgment from the fighter he’s been chasing for more than a year. What’s Next for O’Shaquie Foster? Foster was stellar and he looks every bit the part of a pound-for-pound talent in the sport. With his win on Saturday, Foster is set to face the winner of the upcoming fight between WBA champion Anthony Cacace and Nick Ball. That would be for the undisputed title at 130 pounds. Based on Foster’s performance against Navarrete on Saturday, he’d likely be the favorite against both men. Navarrete vs. Foster Full Results Albert Gonzalez stayed unbeaten and kept his NABF featherweight title on the main card, stopping Edward Vazquez with body shots at 1:04 of the second round. Frank Martin won the vacant NABO super lightweight title with a seventh-round TKO of Tarik Zaina. A scheduled bout between Steven Navarro and Emanuel Moreno was canceled after Navarro missed weight. item.title: Arch Manning, Texas barely save soap opera season with thrilling Ole Miss victory
item.description: Arch Manning, Texas barely save soap opera season with thrilling Ole Miss victory originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Arch Manning crossed his arms after a TD run with fireworks exploding in the background. He stomped around the sideline in defiance. He walked into the end zone for the go-ahead TD. Manning delivered the gotta-have-it game with No. 19 Texas on the brink, even if it was dicey after a second-half comeback by No. 7 Ole Miss. The Longhorns survived in a 34-27 victory. So, this is what we get after Texas coach Steve Sarkisian described Manning as "edgy" this week? It is worth the experience, right? Texas (5-2, 2-2 SEC) jumped out to a three-TD lead on the Rebels (5-2, 3-2 SEC). Manning finished 18 of 30 for 212 yards and three total TDs, albeit with two interceptions and a fumble. He summed up that experience in the postgame interview with ESPN's Holly Rowe. MORE: Which of the SEC 7 two-loss teams has best chance to make CFP? "I think all week we just said, 'Whatever it takes,' and got the win," Manning said. "I think you need to start doing our games more. We're 3-0 with you this year." Those three games were decided by a combined total of seven points. The Longhorns held off a furious comeback led by Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who finished 25 of 52 for 250 yards, two TDs and three interceptions. Chambliss tried to tie the score on the game's final play, but Jelani McDonald, who had the pass breakup on a Hail Mary in the 20-17 victory against Tennessee on Sept. 26, came up with the game-clinching interception. Manning and Texas remain the soap opera of the 2026 season, and this was yet another cliffhanger for the two-loss Longhorns in the jumbled SEC playoff race. MORE: Meet Arch Manning's entire extended family Arch Manning leads Texas to huge halftime lead Here is what we learned after the Longhorns' victory. Backup quarterback KJ Lacey, who was rumored to be in the mix for more first-team reps in the aftermath of Texas' 27-24 loss to Florida in Week 7, will not be the starter this season. Lacey played one snap after Manning took a hard hit in the third quarter. Manning transfer rumors, as they have for the past four years, will fizzle again. Manning could still enter the 2027 NFL Draft and be a first-round pick. Texas' season-long script with Manning, in all its drama, is far from finished. Manning took his own advice and "let it rip" against the Rebels. That started in the first quarter with a 43-yard pass to Ryan Wingo and a 23-yard run by Raleek Brown, who trucked Ole Miss safety Joenel Aguero on the run. Manning scored on a 2-yard run and struck a pose in the end zone. ARCH MANNING TD https://t.co/5d3OzmYzbc — Pick 6 Pack (@Pick6PackFB) October 25, 2026 Manning was not finished. A 19-yard scramble by Manning set up a 50-yard TD pass to Wingo for a 17-3 lead with 12:38 left in the third quarter. Michael Terry III added a 3-yard TD run to extend the lead to 24-3. ARCH MANNING THROWS HIS FIRST TD OF THE GAME 🔥 (via: @espn) https://t.co/bVuW76eaGV — The Sporting News (@sportingnews) October 25, 2026 Manning was 13 of 19 for 171 yards, a TD and an interception in the first half. Chambliss was 6 of 18 for 63 yards and two interceptions, including a fourth-and-goal interception to Texas linebacker Rasheem Biles with 1:37 left in the half. This looked like the game where Manning would silence all the critics. MORE: Where does Steve Sarkisian rank among CFB;s highest paid coaches? Texas survives wild second half This is Texas, after all, which was coming off losses to Oklahoma and Florida the last two weeks. The Sooners and Gators outscored the Longhorns 37-14 in the second half over the last two weeks. Manning lost a fumble on a sack by Blake Purchase, which Kam Franklin recovered in the end zone at the 13:28 mark in the third quarter. The Rebels trimmed the lead to 24-17 on a 6-yard TD pass from Chambliss to Horatio Fields with 6:46 left in the third quarter. The Longhorns had just two first downs in the third quarter. That set up the fourth quarter. Chambliss tied the score with a 27-yard TD pass to Fields with 13:57 left in the fourth quarter. Texas answered with a six-play, 80-yard drive that came exclusively on the ground. Brown had a 47-yard run up the middle, which was the Longhorns' first chunk play of the second half. Terry had runs of 19 and 12 yards, respectively, and Manning walked in a 1-yard TD on a bootleg with 8:04 remaining. ONE OF THE NASTIEST FAKES IN COLLEGE FOOTBALL HISTORY ON THIS TOUCHDOWN PLAY: ARCH MANNING FAKES OUT THE ENTIRE STADIUM AND EVERY DEFENDER ON THE FIELD WITH A FAKE HANDOFF AND A BOOTLEG. INSANE. https://t.co/V1A0JbsQVF — MLFootball (@MLFootball) October 25, 2026 Alex January blocked an Ole Miss field-goal attempt, and Gianni Spetic gave Texas a 34-24 lead on a 33-yard field goal with 2:25 remaining. You knew it wasn't over. Lucas Carneiro kicked a 39-yard field goal, the Rebels recovered the ensuing onside kick and Chambliss nearly led a game-tying drive before the final interception. "I was pacing and said a few prayers, but our defense came up clutch," Manning said. "That's what it's all about." MORE: How a bad day for the Big 12 impacted hurt league's CFP outlook Is Texas back in the playoff mix? The Longhorns still have issues. Edge rusher Colin Simmons (ankle) and running back Hollywood Smothers (shoulder) missed Saturday's game. Tackle Trevor Goosby was carted off with an injury in the first quarter, and receiver Cam Coleman left with a shoulder injury in the third quarter. Texas had 14 penalties for 134 yards. Yet if the College Football Playoff rankings came out Tuesday, the Longhorns would probably be in the top 12 based on victories against Ole Miss, No. 3 Ohio State and No. 11 Tennessee. No other team has three victories against teams inside the top 12 at this point. We'll find out more over the next two weeks in road games against No. 22 Missouri and No. 18 LSU. Texas needs even more out of Manning; otherwise, the doom-and-gloom cycle will start again with a third loss. Is there a more entertaining drama in college football right now?

item.title: Jaylen Brown responds to Jayson Tatum's 'no beef' comments as dispute continues: 'He's got a great PR team'
item.description: Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown are in agreement: there's no beef between the former Boston Celtics teammates. But there might be something, judging from Brown's latest comments. A back-and-forth that began when Brown called cap in an Instagram comment on Tatum's claim he didn't know about his longtime teammate's trade to the Philadelphia 76ers saw the ball land back in Brown's court on Saturday. Following the Sixers' 127-116 win over the Milwaukee Bucks , Brown was asked about Tatum's comments the previous night, specifically "This ain't no f***ing Shaq and Kobe. There's no beef." Brown responded by pointing out that Tatum has a great public relations team, then invoked a different type of meat to describe their relationship : "We've accomplished some great things. He's a hell of a basketball player. He's got a great PR team. There's no beef but it might be a little lamb chops and some gravy. He should stay ready at all times." What does that mean? A reporter asked the natural follow-up question and got this: "That's what it is. No beef. It should never, ever be that. It's just basketball. We both blessed. But it might be a little lamb chop. We'll be alright." When asked if he was willing to have a conversation with Tatum, Brown threw out the great PR team line for a second time and the lamb chop line for a third time: "We both got so much stuff in front of us. At the end of the day, you gotta do what you gotta do for his team. I gotta do what I do for my team. Jayson's a great guy. Like I said, great family. Hell of a basketball player, hell of a PR team. There's no beef. A little lamb chop." Jaylen Brown still has some stuff to say about Jayson Tatum. Emilee Chinn via Getty Images So that's that, we guess, unless Tatum wants to get back into a conversation he very clearly wishes wasn't public, as he said Friday: "It's turned into this drama type of thing. I got two kids. I reached out to him the day he got traded, I called him, I texted him and I understand people process things differently. At this point in our lives, we're too old to be having our relationship discussed X, Y, Z on the internet. If there's a conversation to be had, we can definitely have that conversation. I welcome that. I've always wanted the best for him and wished the best for him. I've always publicly said those things. I see all these things, 'Get your popcorn ready,' like it's a f***ing boxing match. I play basketball." The trade that sent Brown to Philadelphia remains a contentious one. Brown clearly wasn't happy he was being shown the door after a season in which he was the Celtics' clear MVP , while Tatum distanced himself from the decision and said the situation was tough . The pair played nine seasons together and won a championship in 2024, but the Brown trade had an air of inevitability.
