item.title: Comeback kings Brewers down Rays to take 2-0 World Series lead
item.description: Milwaukee's Sal Frelick celebrates after hitting a crucial solo home run in the Brewers' World Series game two defeat of Tampa Bay (JAMIE SQUIRE) The Milwaukee Brewers staged another trademark comeback to defeat the Tampa Bay Rays 5-4 and take a commanding 2-0 lead in the best-of-seven World Series on Saturday. The top-seeded Brewers recovered from 4-0 down after an early Tampa Bay onslaught to complete a rally that edges Milwaukee closer to a first Major League Baseball crown. The win marked the seventh time during this season's playoffs that the Brewers have come from behind to win. Outfielder Sal Frelick blasted a 408-foot home run in the sixth inning to tie it up for Milwaukee at 4-4 before Cooper Pratt's single in the seventh added what turned out to be the winning run for Brice Turang. "As long as there's game left we have a chance -- and I think we've all bought into that," Pratt said. "We're never out of it. And when there's still innings on the board we've still got a chance," Pratt added. Tampa Bay will have the weight of history against them as the series heads back to Florida for game three on Monday. Only 10 teams have ever recovered from 2-0 down to win the World Series. Rays manager Kevin Cash believes home-field advantage for the next three games could give Tampa Bay a path back into the series. "These Milwaukee fans have been really loud. I know our fans are going to be really loud and excited to see us come back and kind of reset ourselves a little bit," Cash said. "We've got a really good pitcher going, as do they. A lot of confidence in this club to respond. They've done it all season long and they'll continue to do it." The Rays surged into a commanding 4-0 lead in the top of the first inning with Yandy Diaz scooting to second base after a throwing error by Brewers shortstop Pratt. Chandler Simpson singled soon afterwards to bring Diaz home and give the Rays a 1-0 lead. Simpson then used his speed to steal second base and when Junior Caminero drove into the left field, Simpson raced home to score. The Rays made it 4-0 when catcher Liam Hicks bludgeoned a towering 411-foot two-run homer into the upper deck of right center-field to further rock the Brewers. Milwaukee were quick to hit back in the bottom of the inning, with William Contreras singling on a ground ball to score Jackson Chourio. Garrett Mitchell's single to right field allowed Jake Bauers to score to trim the Rays advantage to two runs. Milwaukee knocked Tampa Bay starter Drew Rasmussen out of the game in the fourth inning and then pounced with Frelick's home run in the sixth, before Pratt's single in the seventh gave the Brewers the lead. Brewers reliever Aaron Ashby grabbed the final five outs to secure victory. rcw/pst
item.content:encoded: Milwaukee's Sal Frelick celebrates after hitting a crucial solo home run in the Brewers' World Series game two defeat of Tampa Bay (JAMIE SQUIRE) The Milwaukee Brewers staged another trademark comeback to defeat the Tampa Bay Rays 5-4 and take a commanding 2-0 lead in the best-of-seven World Series on Saturday. The top-seeded Brewers recovered from 4-0 down after an early Tampa Bay onslaught to complete a rally that edges Milwaukee closer to a first Major League Baseball crown. The win marked the seventh time during this season's playoffs that the Brewers have come from behind to win. Outfielder Sal Frelick blasted a 408-foot home run in the sixth inning to tie it up for Milwaukee at 4-4 before Cooper Pratt's single in the seventh added what turned out to be the winning run for Brice Turang. "As long as there's game left we have a chance -- and I think we've all bought into that," Pratt said. "We're never out of it. And when there's still innings on the board we've still got a chance," Pratt added. Tampa Bay will have the weight of history against them as the series heads back to Florida for game three on Monday. Only 10 teams have ever recovered from 2-0 down to win the World Series. Rays manager Kevin Cash believes home-field advantage for the next three games could give Tampa Bay a path back into the series. "These Milwaukee fans have been really loud. I know our fans are going to be really loud and excited to see us come back and kind of reset ourselves a little bit," Cash said. "We've got a really good pitcher going, as do they. A lot of confidence in this club to respond. They've done it all season long and they'll continue to do it." The Rays surged into a commanding 4-0 lead in the top of the first inning with Yandy Diaz scooting to second base after a throwing error by Brewers shortstop Pratt. Chandler Simpson singled soon afterwards to bring Diaz home and give the Rays a 1-0 lead. Simpson then used his speed to steal second base and when Junior Caminero drove into the left field, Simpson raced home to score. The Rays made it 4-0 when catcher Liam Hicks bludgeoned a towering 411-foot two-run homer into the upper deck of right center-field to further rock the Brewers. Milwaukee were quick to hit back in the bottom of the inning, with William Contreras singling on a ground ball to score Jackson Chourio. Garrett Mitchell's single to right field allowed Jake Bauers to score to trim the Rays advantage to two runs. Milwaukee knocked Tampa Bay starter Drew Rasmussen out of the game in the fourth inning and then pounced with Frelick's home run in the sixth, before Pratt's single in the seventh gave the Brewers the lead. Brewers reliever Aaron Ashby grabbed the final five outs to secure victory. rcw/pst

Talladega Superspeedway is known to be chaotic, with multi-line drafts and side-by-side racing at nearly 200mph that always makes for some precarious conditions. With the uncertainty of this track, it's completely possible that an underdog could secure a clutch win. item.title: Rockets’ Alperen Sengun rattles the rim with insane slam dunk vs. Hawks
item.description: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Rockets’ Alperen Sengun rattles the rim with insane slam dunk vs. Hawks appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Houston Rockets are flying high after their dramatic win over the San Antonio Spurs, which saw them improve to 2-0. They had sights set on win No. 3 Saturday against the Atlanta Hawks, and Alperen Sengun was more than doing his part. Early in the third quarter, the Turkish big man decided to take the ball down the court against “The Great Barrier Thief” himself, Dyson Daniels. Sengun then decided to do it all by himself as he drove past Daniels and threw down a slam dunk through traffic. ALPEREN SENGUN RISES UP FOR THE HUGE SLAM 😤 pic.twitter.com/klOSWq8Rds Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 25, 2026 Sengun has had a strong start to the season for the Rockets. Over the first two games, he’s averaged 26.0 points, 8.5 rebounds and 6.0 assists . And he kept up his fine overall play against the Hawks. He finished with 17 points, nine rebounds, and seven assists to lead the Rockets to a 121-114 win. Point guard Fred VanVleet was rested on the second night of a back-to-back , but the newfound balance in the Rockets offense continued against Atlanta. Seven Houston players had 11 or more points, led by Kevin Durant’s 22. The return of VanVleet has been a welcome addition to Sengun, who no longer has to have quite as much responsibility as a facilitator on offense. But as he showed with his amazing drive and dunk against the Hawks, he is still more than capable of calling his own number and putting the ball on the floor at times. The Rockets will take on the Hawks again, this time in Atlanta, for the second half of their home-and-home on Monday. Related: Rockets-Hawks injury report features multiple questionable players Related: Rockets’ Amen Thompson calls game with insane block on Victor Wembanyama

item.title: Austin FC rallies to beat Sporting KC, keep slim MLS playoff hopes alive
item.description: HOUSTON, TEXAS - JULY 25: Myrto Uzuni #10 of the Austin FC looks to pass the ball against the Houston Dynamo FC during second half at Shell Energy Stadium on July 25, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Maria Lysaker/Getty Images) (Maria Lysaker/Getty Images) One down, three to go - and some help - for Austin FC . The Verde and Black's MLS playoff hopes hinge on a four-game winning streak and a lot of friendly results elsewhere around the league to end the year, but Austin FC took the first step in that unlikely process Saturday. Myrto Uzuni scored twice in the final 30 minutes as the Verde and Black rallied for a 2-1 win over Sporting Kansas City at Sporting Park in Kansas City, Kansas. Uzuni now has 13 goals across all competitions, including nine in MLS play, which leads the club. It was a mostly good showing for Austin FC, though it was a bit lucky in the final 15 minutes when Kansas City failed to finish some chances, most notably Stephen Afrifa sending a shot inside the Verde and Black's six-yard box wide of the goal. Austin FC had 56% of possession and finished with an expected goals stat of 1.77, according to the Apple TV broadcast. The club also won with backup goalie Damian Las playing. Afrifa put Kansas City ahead early in the second half with a well-taken shot in the box. Austin FC (8-13-10, 34 points, 14th West) plays Wednesday at home against Real Salt Lake. item.title: Kochetkov Earns Shutout – Hurricanes 4, Blues 0
item.description: ST. LOUIS, MO - OCTOBER 24: Carolina Hurricanes goaltender Pyotr Kochetkov (52) makes a glove save on the breakaway shot by St. Louis Blues left wing Connor McMichael (77) during an NHL regular season game where the St. Louis Blues hosted the Carolina Hurricanes on Saturday October 24th, 2026, at the Enterprise Center in St. Louis MO (Photo by Rick Ulreich/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Pyotr Kochetkov improved his record to 7-0-0 with a 24 save shutout and the Carolina Hurricanes defeated the St. Louis Blues on Saturday night, 4-0. The Hurricanes now have a 9-2-2 record and their 20 points put them at first place in the league, (for now). The Canes finished up their road trip with a 3-1-1 record and will return home for their next game Tuesday night. After a scoreless first period, the visiting team broke through for three goals in the second. Sean Walker got the party started four minutes and change into the period off of another sterling assist by Jackson Blake. Just 20 seconds later, Jordan Martinook found Jesperi Kotkaniemi and “KK” made no mistake to put his team up, 2-0. Speaking of Kotkaniemi, he also had a team high 63% faceoff percentage, (10 of 16). His goal was the third of the season for him. He has been playing better and better since having more of a chance. Kochetkov now has 12 shutouts in his career. Later in the second period, Seth Jarvis found Logan Stankoven on a breakaway and Stankoven buried his 8th of the season. In the third period, Carolina finished off the scoring when Nikolaj Ehlers knocked in a powerplay goal. It was the only powerplay chance of the night for the Hurricanes. They successfully killed the only opportunity that the Blues had with the advantage. The Canes outshot the Blues in every period and finished up with 39-24 advantage. The Hurricanes will take Sunday off before returning to practice on Monday. Game Summary – https://www.nhl.com/scores/htmlreports/20262027/GS020175.HTM Event Summary – https://www.nhl.com/scores/htmlreports/20262027/ES020175.HTM

item.title: Everyone Gets a Shot: Kochetkov Leads Hurricanes to Shutout Win Over Blues in Conclusion of Road Trip
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Western Conference road trip is done! The Carolina Hurricanes came out of the five-game journey with seven points, finishing things off with their win over the St. Louis Blues. Fascinatingly, in their win, every player on the Hurricanes recorded at least one shot on goal – unsurprisingly led by Logan Stankoven, who forced goaltender Joel Hofer to make five saves, and perhaps surprisingly, his shot count was tied with the bottom line’s centerman, Skyler Brind’Amour, who also had five shots. …Okay, one player did not have a shot on goal, and that was goaltender Pyotr Kochetkov – but he was certainly the man of the night as he finished the game with a perfect sheet, not allowing a single goal in the Hurricanes’ 4-0 win. Let’s get into the action, shall we? The first period of the game didn’t see a single goal despite chances on both ends of the ice, but the second frame wouldn’t be the same case. Scoring just 20 seconds apart were Sean Walker and Jesperi Kotkaniemi – Walker’s goal assisted by Jackson Blake for his 100th career NHL point. And the Carolina Hurricanes get the first goal of the game–the first goal of the season for Sean Walker! (AND the 100th NHL point of Jackson Blake for real this time! I didn't get mixed up again! XD) #CarolinaCulture #STLBlues #NHL pic.twitter.com/dqmnwJJOrA — Queen of the Puck (@rbarkleyhockey) October 25, 2026 Then, a little over midway through the game, Stankoven scored on an extension of the penalty kill, with a little helper by Seth Jarvis – his second of the night after assisting Kotkaniemi. On an extension of the penalty kill, Seth Jarvis deals an apple and Logan Stankoven wires a shot past Joel Hofer👏👏👏 #CarolinaCulture #STLBlues #NHL pic.twitter.com/pfeqVqETPO — Queen of the Puck (@rbarkleyhockey) October 25, 2026 Early in the third period, Nikolaj Ehlers caught the attention of fans and media after he went to assist Kochetkov with the straps on his pads during a stoppage in play – jokingly being called an equipment manager. Hilariously, he was called that yet again by broadcaster Tripp Tracy when he scored moments later on the power play. "From fixing a goaltender's strap to probably delivering a dagger" The Carolina Hurricanes are up 4-0 thanks to a power play goal from 'Equipment Manager Nikolaj Ehlers' #CarolinaCulture #STLBlues #NHL https://t.co/omdj7Phrbo pic.twitter.com/y9JNUHBW3D — Queen of the Puck (@rbarkleyhockey) October 25, 2026 When the game concluded , Kochetkov had made a 24-save shutout, including swallowing 11 high-danger slot chances. Extending his season-opening winning streak to seven games, he has claimed the second best start in a season in franchise history, and the fourth longest winning streak to start a season leaguewide in the last ten years. The Carolina Hurricanes overcame the St. Louis Blues with a 4-0 shutout courtesy of goaltender Pyotr Kochetkov, who was given his headpats and huggies as the team showed him their gratitude, as is traditi

item.title: Aaron Ashby approaches history with latest dominant performance for Brewers
item.description: Aaron Ashby approaches history with latest dominant performance for Brewers originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Milwaukee Brewers are now two wins away from their first World Series title, thanks to an unlikely hero. Lefty reliever Aaron Ashby has been a reliable reliever in the past three seasons, but he has completely dominated the competition this postseason. Ashby has been the Brewers' best reliever, over closer Trevor Megill, and it showed in Milwaukee's Game 2 win on Saturday night. Manager Pat Murphy trusted Ashby to get the final five outs in a 5-4 win over the Tampa Bay Rays instead of turning to Megill. That remained the case even when Ashby allowed a leadoff double in the ninth inning, and even when the dangerous Yandy Diaz was at the plate. item.title: ‘What a disgusting disgusting offense’: Dave Portnoy tells Michigan coach to ‘go get a plane ticket to the moon’ after loss
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Michigan Wolverines suffered a disappointing loss to the Indiana Hoosiers on Saturday, despite several chances to put the visitors away. The Wolverines’ defense came to play, holding the No. 6-ranked team to 13 points in an overtime loss; instead, their offense and its coordinator may be to blame. Michigan lost 13-6 after a disappointing overtime battle, and fans and critics are beyond disappointed with the “disgusting” display of football the Wolverines have shown recently. Barstool founder and notorious Wolverines fan Dave Portnoy immediately took to social media to rip Michigan’s offensive coordinator, Jason Beck, saying he felt the team’s loss was ultimately on him. “They’re too talented on offense to be this pathetic,” Portnoy said via X . “It doesn’t matter; I think Bryce Underwood probably gives us the best chance to win, and he was a scapegoat. Bryce Underwood was a scapegoat for Jason Beck. “Jason Beck is horrific. Jason Beck is the worst offensive play caller, worst offensive coordinator I’ve ever watched with these eyes. Jason Beck, get him out. If you want to, just make him the water boy. Take the play calling away from Jason Beck; Jason Beck doesn’t know what the f*** he’s doing. Jason Beck is disgusting.” Portnoy didn’t blame the players; instead, he blamed the coaches. Michigan started freshman quarterback Tommy Carr over Bryce Underwood, and the Wolverines struggled in the red zone on Saturday. Facing third-and-1 from the Indiana 1-yard line, Beck called a naked bootleg, and Carr was sacked for a 13-yard loss. The drive was then squandered on a missed field goal by kicker Trey Butkowski. Although the sack and the miss were blown plays by two specific players, the play calling from Beck leading up to those moments is something fans like Portnoy can’t comprehend. “They played hard, Michigan, but what a disgusting, disgusting offense and disgusting, disgusting game to watch. Defense plays their nuts off; defense deserves a win. But Jason Beck, go get a plane ticket to the f***ing moon and let’s shoot you there.” During a postgame press conference, head coach Kyle Whittingham shielded Beck from media bullets while taking accountability for the poor play calling. “Everything falls on my shoulders, so whatever happens in the course of a game is on me,” Whittingham said, via Sports Illustrated . “That was not a good football call, no, that was not a good call at that point in time. “I have the ability to overrule anything in the whole program. And so, like I said, it circles back to me, but it was a very disappointing outcome and a call that I know Jason wishes he had back, because it really was damaging.” Next weekend, Michigan will travel to New Jersey to face the Rutgers Scarlet Knights, hoping to redeem their season. item.title: No. 25 Wildcats claw Cyclones
item.description: Dubuque native Kyle Konrardy (97) kicks a field goal during the first half of a football game between the Iowa State Cyclones and the University of Arizona Wildcats on October 24, 2026 at Casino Del Sol Stadium in Tucson. | ﻿Christopher Hook/Icon Sportswire TUCSON, Ariz. — Quarterbacks Jaylen Raynor and Connor Moberly combined for 169 passing yards, but Iowa State struggled to maintain offensive traction on the ground in a 39-3 loss to Arizona on Saturday at Casino Del Sol Stadium. The Cyclones (3-4, 1-3) were limited to 221 total yards of offense and 14 first downs while being kept out of the end zone throughout the contest. Arizona (6-1, 3-1) controlled the tempo with 477 total yards, led by quarterback Noah Fifita, who completed 27 of 34 passes for 308 yards and two touchdowns. Arizona set an aggressive tone early, taking an 8-0 lead just 31 seconds into the game when Fifita connected with Isaiah Mizell on a 71-yard touchdown pass, followed by a two-point conversion pass to Tyler Powell. The Wildcats expanded their lead to 15-0 later in the opening quarter on a 6-yard touchdown run by Quincy Craig. Iowa State answered with its most effective drive of the quarter, marching 53 yards in seven plays. The possession was sparked by a 32-yard completion from Raynor to tight end Vince Benetti down to the Arizona 14-yard line. After Raynor was sacked for a 10-yard loss by Malcolm Hartzog and Dominic Lolesio, Kyle Konrardy got the Cyclones on the board with a 40-yard field goal with 1:06 remaining in the first quarter. The Cyclones engineered another promising drive early in the second quarter, driving 55 yards in eight plays to reach the Arizona 20-yard line. Raynor jump-started the advance with a 17-yard pass to Omari Hayes and a 27-yard completion to Jamal Polite, advancing the ball to the Wildcats’ 29-yard line. Raynor then connected with Easton Miller for 5 yards to setup third-and-short, but after a 2-yard pass to Ty Claiborne on fourth down fell short of the line to gain, Iowa State turned the ball over on downs at the 20. Arizona capitalized with a 15-play, 80-yard drive capped by Kedrick Reescano’s 5-yard touchdown run. In the final two minutes of the half, Raynor completed passes of 8 yards to Claiborne and 12 yards to Cody Jackson, aided by a 15-yard pass interference penalty on Dwight Bootle II. However, Raynor fumbled on a scramble at the Arizona 49-yard line, recovered by Tyrese Boss. Arizona’s Michael Salgado-Medina missed a 31-yard field goal attempt as time expired in the half with Arizona leading 25-3. Defensive execution dominated the third quarter, which ended completely scoreless. Moberly opened the half under center for Iowa State, completing a 12-yard pass to Hayes and later connecting with Miller for an 18-yard gain to cross midfield. Moberly opened the half under center for Iowa State, completing a 12-yard pass to Hayes and later connecting with Miller for an 18-yard gain to cross midfield. Cornerback Keyon Washington delivered a highlight for the Cyclone defense by forcing a fumble on Arizona’s Caleb Smith, which bounced out of bounds. A 5-yard penalty on Iowa State for running into the kicker on a fake punt extended an Arizona drive, but the Cyclones held firm to force a Chase Ridley punt. Iowa State opened the final quarter with a 13-play, 36-yard drive highlighted by an 8-yard rush from Aiden Flora and a 6-yard scramble by Moberly. After a punt, the Cyclones regained possession down 32-3 following a 40-yard touchdown pass from Fifita to Henry Gabalis. Moberly ripped off a 12-yard run to the ISU 37 and completed a 5-yard pass to Benetti. However, back-to-back incompletions and a 7-yard sack by Dash Fifita ended the possession on downs at the Iowa State 36-yard line. Arizona backup quarterback Sawyer Anderson concluded the scoring with a 4-yard touchdown run with 1:55 remaining. Iowa State’s final drive featured a 6-yard rush by Ryver Peppers before Nela Taliauli recorded a 4-yard sack to force a final punt. Raynor completed 8 of 10 passes for 106 yards, while Moberly went 7 for 17 for 63 yards through the air and added 35 gross rushing yards (20 net). Flora paced the Cyclone rushing attack with 36 yards on 12 carries. Benetti finished as Iowa State’s leading receiver with three catches for 42 yards, while Hayes added two receptions for 29 yards, Polite caught one pass for 27 yards and Miller recorded two catches for 23 yards. Linebacker Sullivan Schlimgen anchored the Iowa State defense with a game high 15 total tackles, including a sack and two tackles for loss. Carson Willich recorded 10 tackles.

item.title: Frelick homer sparks Brewers rally for 2-0 World Series lead over Rays
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers right fielder Sal Frelick hits a solo home run against the Tampa Bay Rays in the sixth inning of Game 2 of the 2026 World Series on Saturday at American Family Field in Milwaukee. Photo by Tannen Maury/UPI Oct. 24 (UPI) -- Sal Frelick whipped his wrists through the zone and splintered a fastball over the center field fence for a near-earthquake-triggering. game-tying home run, guiding a thrilling Milwaukee Brewers rally past the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 2 of the World Series on Saturday in Milwaukee. The Brewers, who trailed 4-0 in the first inning, leaned on a dominant bullpen as their bats warmed throughout the 5-4 victory at American Field Field. With their seventh comeback win this postseason, they moved within two victories of their first World Series crown. "Regardless of if we are down or up, that chip-away mentality is just how our offense is designed," Frelick said on the Fox broadcast. Each team packed the base paths with early traffic, but the Rays capitalized most off that live lumber. Left fielder Chandler Simpson drove in designated hitter Yandy Diaz for Game 2's first run in the first inning. Third baseman Junior Caminero plated Simpson with a single in the next at-bat. Catcher Liam Hicks followed with a 411-foot, two-run homer to give the Rays a lead they kept until the sixth inning. Milwaukee Brewers outfielder Sal Frelick runs the bases after hitting a solo home run against the Tampa Bay Rays in the sixth inning of Game 2 of the 2026 World Series on Saturday at American Family Field in Milwaukee. Photo by Tannen Maury/UPI But the early electricity shorted, as Brewers pitchers did not allow another run. The Brewers cut the deficit in half through RBI singles from catcher William Contreras and center fielder Garrett Mitchell off Rays ace Drew Rasmussen in the bottom of the first frame. Brewers shortstop Cooper Pratt scored a third Brewers run off a fielding error in the fourth. Milwaukee Brewers center fielder Garrett Mitchell hits an RBI single against the Tampa Bay Rays in the first inning of Game 2 of the 2026 World Series on Saturday at American Family Field in Milwaukee. Photo by Tannen Maury/UPI Frelick tied the score when he led off the bottom of the sixth with his 408-foot solo shot off relief pitcher Ian Seymour. Pratt returned for his go-ahead RBI single in the seventh off Tyler Wells. Bullpen arms JoJo Romero, Dustin May, DL Hall, Abner Uribe and Aaron Ashby combined to allow just four hits and no runs over the final six innings. Tampa Bay Rays left fielder Chandler Simpson falls trying to catch a single from Milwaukee Brewers designated hitter Christian Yelich in the sixth inning of Game 2 of the 2026 World Series on Saturday at American Family Field in Milwaukee. Photo by Tannen Maury/UPI "As long as there's game left, we have a chance," Pratt said. "I think we've all bought into that." The Rays threatened with a final base runner in the top of the ninth, but Ashby cemented the triumph with a game-endi

Photo by Tannen Maury/UPI "It was just about making pitches," Ashby said. Brewers right-handed pitcher Logan Henderson allowed three hits and four runs, including three earned, over the first three frames. Rasmussen allowed six hits and three runs over 3 2/3 innings. Frelick, Contreras and left fielder Jackson Chourio collected two hits apiece for the Brewers. Center fielder Jonny DeLuca, who went 2 for 4, was the only Rays player to log more than one hit. The Rays (0-2) will host the Brewers (2-0) in Game 3 of the best-of-seven game series at 8 p.m. EDT Monday at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Fla.. They will host Game 4 at the same time there Tuesday.

item.title: No. 15 Florida State soccer takes first ACC loss against No. 17 Notre Dame
item.description: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - DECEMBER 8: Brian Pensky of the Florida State Seminoles stands for the national anthem before the Division I Women's Soccer Championship against the Stanford Cardinal held at CPKC Stadium on December 8, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by C. Morgan Engel/NCAA Photos via Getty Images) | NCAA Photos via Getty Images No. 15 Florida State women’s soccer fell 2-0 to No. 17 Notre Dame on Saturday night in Tallahassee, ending the Seminoles’ two-game winning streak. With the loss, Florida State took its first conference loss and fell to 7-2-3, while Notre Dame improved to 7-1-6. Florida State’s starting 11 included Shaneil Buckley, Wrianna Hudson, Sam Erbach, Peyton McGovern, Joelle Jung, Nyanya Touray, Nawreen Ahmad, Bridget Mutipula, Janet Okeke, Grace Hoytink and Kate Ockene. The Seminoles struggled to create offensive opportunities in the first half, while Notre Dame was able to take an early lead. The Fighting Irish opened the scoring in the 15th minute, taking a 1-0 lead. Notre Dame continued to control much of the first half, finishing with five shots, including two on goal, while FSU was unable to record a shot before halftime. The Fighting Irish carried their momentum into the second half, with Izzy Engle scoring just 47 seconds into the second half to extend Notre Dame’s lead to 2-0. Florida State began creating more offensive opportunities shortly after, with Tanner Strickland recording the Seminoles’ first shot on goal in the 48th minute. Hoytink had another opportunity in the next minute for FSU, but her shot went just wide to the left. Buckley also created a scoring opportunity, but her shot was blocked by Notre Dame’s defense. In the 64th minute, Ahmad found Hudson with a pass that led to another shot opportunity for the Seminoles, but FSU was unable to convert. Hudson continued to pressure Notre Dame’s defense, coming close to scoring with a header in the 82nd minute that missed the goal. Despite creating more opportunities in the second half, Florida State was unable to find the back of the net. The Seminoles finished with six shots, including three on goal, while Notre Dame recorded eight shots, with four on goal. Florida State will look to bounce back when it hosts Duke on Thursday, Oct. 29, with kickoff set for 8 p.m.

item.title: Cowboys Get Stunning Dak Prescott Trade Take From Skip Bayless
item.description: Dallas Cowboys QB Dak Prescott had a strong message for an AT&T Stadiumw order after he called the team's performance "embarrassing" on Thursday Getty Skip Bayless has grown frustrated with the Dallas Cowboys’ uneven start and said he would immediately swap starting quarterback Dak Prescott for Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels. The Cowboys sit at 2-4 after six games in the 2026 season, most recently falling 23-13 to the Green Bay Packers. Prescott has drawn criticism during the stretch, including after a 24-16 home loss to the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Bayless, a longtime Cowboys supporter, made the remarks on the Gridiron podcast alongside Aqib Talib. He pointed to the team’s results with Prescott available in recent seasons. Skip Bayless Open to Straight-Up Dak Prescott Deal for Jayden Daniels In the clip shared by Gridiron on X, Bayless made his opinion crystal clear. “If they want to trade me Jayden Daniels for Dak Prescott. It’s done. Straight up, player for player. Let me have him, I’ll take it,” Bayless said . “He was available all last year when we went 7-9-1. He’s been available this year; we’re 2-4. Give me Jayden Daniels.” Daniels, in his third season, has started four games for the Commanders this year. He has completed 75 of 116 passes for 759 yards, five touchdowns and zero interceptions, posting a 97.6 passer rating. He has also rushed for 213 yards and two scores. Prescott has started all six games for Dallas. He is 163 of 246 for 1,639 yards, 10 touchdowns and five interceptions with a 90.1 rating and 66.3 percent completion rate. The Cowboys rank sixth in the league in passing yards per game at 273.2 but sit near the bottom of the league in rushing. Division Race and Monday Night Matchup The Cowboys face the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night in Week 7. Philadelphia is also 2-4, and a Dallas victory would move the Cowboys into a tie for second in the NFC East. The New York Giants lead the division at 3-2-1, while the Commanders are 1-4-1. Dallas finished 7-9-1 last season with Prescott under center for most of the year. Daniels, as a rookie in 2024, helped the Commanders reach the NFC Championship Game. The Cowboys have not advanced beyond the divisional round during Prescott’s tenure as the full-time starter since 2016. Prescott’s recent outings include a 34-of-54, 258-yard performance with one touchdown and two interceptions against Green Bay. Against Tampa Bay he went 24 of 42 for 316 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the loss that snapped the Buccaneers’ winless streak. The Cowboys’ defense has allowed 26.5 points per game and ranks near the bottom of the league against the run. Offense has produced 25.2 points per game, but turnovers have been an issue in the losses. Bayless has long argued that Dallas needs a different approach at quarterback after years of regular-season production without deep playoff runs. The team remains in contention in a weak NFC East, with games remaining

item.title: SEC college football playoff outlook: Dissecting logjam of 2-loss teams in contested league
item.description: SEC college football playoff outlook: Dissecting logjam of 2-loss teams in contested league originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . If you're looking for some clarity on which teams are legitimate College Football Playoff threats inside the SEC, Week 8 made a mess of things. After Saturday, we now have multiple two-loss teams inside the conference that will be a mess to sort out. On Saturday, No. 11 Tennessee suffered its second loss of the season to South Carolina on the road, and No. 4 Ole Miss lost 34-27 in a thriller to No. 19 Texas in Austin. No. 18 LSU improved to 6-2 with a 38-17 win over Auburn on the road, and No. 13 Alabama got a victory over Texas A&M, 31-20. There are also two-loss teams in the SEC in Missouri, Florida and Georgia, which all had byes this week. Here's an attempt at sorting out the logjam that is the SEC, which has multiple two-loss teams that appear to be in the hunt for the College Football Playoff after Week 8. MORE: Bad Day for the Big 12: How bad losses by Texas Tech, BYU hurt conference's CFP outlook SEC teams with 2 losses No. 7 Ole Miss Rebels (5-2) Ole Miss got its first signature win with a 32-24 victory over then-No. 7 LSU in Week 3. The Rebels also have ranked wins over Louisville and a 31-3 win over then-No. 13 Missouri last week. Ole Miss' first loss came on the road against Florida, but the Gators were ranked No. 21 at the time and are back in the rankings after a win over Texas on the road last week. Ole Miss also defeated Vanderbilt on the road, 52-17. Against Texas, the Rebels did come back from a 24-3 deficit at halftime and tied the game early in the fourth quarter. The Rebels even responded after going down 10 late, scoring a field goal with 1:22 left, and a recovered onside kick gave Trinidad Chambliss a chance at a Hail Mary that Texas held off. The committee won't fault Ole Miss for losing on the road too much, but the Rebels can't afford to stumble. Ole Miss has just one ranked team remaining on its schedule, as it is set to play No. 5 Georgia on Nov. 7. Elsewhere in the SEC, Ole Miss draws Auburn and Mississippi State at home and goes on the road to play Oklahoma on Nov. 14. If the Rebels win out, a CFP bid is likely. Three losses, even against a very good team in Georgia, make it seem unlikely. MORE: Why did NC State fire Dave Doeren? As for the losses, Alabama lost to No. 2 Georgia on a last-second field goal and fell 26-10 on the road to Tennessee last week. The committee likely won't fault the Tide for either of their losses. If you're looking for some clarity on which teams are legitimate College Football Playoff threats inside the SEC, Week 8 made a mess of things. After Saturday, we now have multiple two-loss teams inside the conference that will be a mess to sort out. No. 18 LSU improved to 6-2 with a 38-17 win over Auburn on the road, and No. 13 Alabama got a victory over Texas A&M, 31-20. There are also two-loss teams in the SEC in Missouri, Florida and Georgia, which all had byes this week. Here's an attempt at sorting out the logjam that is the SEC, which has multiple two-loss teams that appear to be in the hunt for the College Football Playoff after Week 8. MORE: Bad Day for the Big 12: How bad losses by Texas Tech, BYU hurt conference's CFP outlook SEC teams with 2 losses No. 7 Ole Miss Rebels (5-2) Ole Miss got its first signature win with a 32-24 victory over then-No. 7 LSU in Week 3. The Rebels also have ranked wins over Louisville and a 31-3 win over then-No. 13 Missouri last week. Ole Miss' first loss came on the road against Florida, but the Gators were ranked No. 21 at the time and are back in the rankings after a win over Texas on the road last week. Ole Miss also defeated Vanderbilt on the road, 52-17. Against Texas, the Rebels did come back from a 24-3 deficit at halftime and tied the game early in the fourth quarter. The Rebels even responded after going down 10 late, scoring a field goal with 1:22 left, and a recovered onside kick gave Trinidad Chambliss a chance at a Hail Mary that Texas held off. The committee won't fault Ole Miss for losing on the road too much, but the Rebels can't afford to stumble. Ole Miss has just one ranked team remaining on its schedule, as it is set to play No. 5 Georgia on Nov. 7. Elsewhere in the SEC, Ole Miss draws Auburn and Mississippi State at home and goes on the road to play Oklahoma on Nov. 14. If the Rebels win out, a CFP bid is likely. Three losses, even against a very good team in Georgia, make it seem unlikely. MORE: Why did NC State fire Dave Doeren? No. 13 Alabama Crimson Tide (6-2) Alabama has a strong resume, with road wins over Kentucky and Mississippi State. The Tide also have conference wins over South Carolina and Texas A&M, including a 48-10 Week 1 win over East Carolina. As for the losses, Alabama lost to No. 2 Georgia on a last-second field goal and fell 26-10 on the road to Tennessee last week. The committee likely won't fault the Tide for either of their losses. But Alabama cannot afford to lose to any of its remaining opponents: LSU in Baton Rouge on Nov. 7, Vanderbilt, Chattanooga or Auburn at home for the Iron Bowl. If the Tide win on the road against LSU, it would almost guarantee a bid, assuming they win out. No. 18 LSU Tigers (6-2) LSU beat Clemson 58-10 in Week 1, and although Dabo Swinney's team wasn't ranked, the committee will value a big nonconference win like that. LSU also beat Louisiana Tech and McNeese State outside of the SEC. As for the Tigers' conference wins, they have some solid ones, such as a 35-6 win over Texas A&M when the Aggies were ranked at the time and a win over then-No. 16 Mississippi State. On Saturday, LSU went on the road and beat Auburn, which just beat Georgia last week, 38-17. LSU's losses don't look terrible. The first was on the road to Ole Miss, which the Tigers had a chance to beat late. The other was also on the road, against Kentucky, which looks like one of the best surprise teams in the SEC. The Tigers have a tough remaining slate, featuring three straight ranked opponents: Alabama and Texas at home on Nov. 7 and 8, respectively, and a road trip to Tennessee on Nov. 21. LSU closes out the season against 3-4 Arkansas on the road. MORE: Explaineing the chaotic, controversial and thrilling ending to UCF's upset of BYU No. 19 Texas Longhorns (5-2) Texas' CFP resume is a mess, to say the least. The Longhorns' best win came in Week 2, with a come-from-behind win over then-No. 1 Ohio State. Texas also defeated then-No. 14 Tennessee on the road 20-17, including non-conference wins over Texas State and UTSA. The Longhorns' two losses are puzzling, both to unranked teams in Oklahoma and Florida at home. Texas' Arch Manning threw two interceptions against a struggling Sooners team. The next week, Texas lost at home to an unranked Florida which had lost back-to-back games to Missouri and South Carolina. But with a huge 34-27 home win over a very good Ole Miss team, the Longhorns are still alive. Texas has remaining home conference games against unranked Mississippi State and Arkansas, and goes on the road to play No. 22 Missouri and No. 18 LSU next month. The Longhorns will end the regular season on the road against Texas A&M. While Texas would be in with two losses, the win over Ohio State earlier in the season might give Texas a case with three losses, depending on how the Buckeyes finish No. 11 Tennessee Vols (6-2) Tennessee's case took a hit on Saturday, as the Vols were upset 27-24 on the road against unranked South Carolina on Saturday. The Vols' only other loss came at home, a close 20-17 one to Texas in a game that Tennessee was very much in. The Vols' biggest signature win came two weeks ago, beating then-No. 6 Alabama 26-10 at home. Tennessee also has wins over Georgia Tech and Arkansas on the road, as well as a conference win over Auburn. The Vols have two ranked teams still to play, including at home vs. No. 7 Kentucky next week, and a home game against LSU on Nov. 21. Tennessee also plays at Texas A&M and Vanderbilt, but the Vols should be heavy favorites in both those games. MORE: How bad Week 8 losses by Texas Tech, BYU impact Big 12's CFP outlook No. 20 Florida Gators (5-2) The Florida Gators are the most confusing team in the entire SEC. Florida burst into the CFP picture with its dominant 52-38 win over then-No. 4 Ole Miss at home in Week 4. The Gators then dropped back-to-back games on the road to Missouri and lost to a three-loss, unranked South Carolina team at home. The Gators then went on the road last week and upset Texas, winning 27-24. Just how good this Florida team is will come down to how it does the rest of the season. The Gators biggest test is next week, taking on No. 5 Georgia in Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Ga. Florida also has to go on the road to play Kentucky on Nov. 14. Florida then has remaining home conference games against Oklahoma and Vanderbilt, and plays rival Florida State on the road to close out the regular season. No. 22 Missouri Tigers (5-2) Missouri might be the team least likely to make the field, thanks to what it's done so far and what it still has in front of it. The Tigers beat non-conference Kansas 38-21 in Week 2, and took down then-No. 8 Florida at home on Oct. 3. The Tigers also beat Texas A&M 27-6 at home, with losses to ranked conference opponents in Mississippi State and Ole Miss. Missouri has a brutal stretch next month, featuring games against No. 19 Texas, at No. 5 Georgia and vs. No. 12 Kentucky at home before a regular-season home finale against Oklahoma. However unlikely, the Tigers will likely be in the hunt if it makes it out of that stretch undefeated. item.title: USC falls apart in Madison, losing to unranked Wisconsin
item.description: Lincoln Riley and his USC Trojans headed into the bye week with serious optimism after knocking off Penn State in front of over 114,000 Nittany Lion fans wearing white. On Saturday evening, however, a complete 180. The Trojans fell flat on their faces at Camp Randall Stadium, losing 24-7 to the Wisconsin Badgers. Chances of an appearance in the College Football Playoff are now close to none, with USC almost certainly needing to run the table through its final four games. Unfortunately for them, three of those matchups will come against Ohio State, Indiana and UCLA. "Just flat-out didn't play good enough on any of the three sides of the ball," Riley said after the loss. "Didn't coach good enough, made critical errors on the road...I take responsibility for it. It's hard to win on the road, and you have to play a lot better than we did tonight." It started with an offensive unit that had perhaps its worst display since Riley took over as head coach of the program. item.content:encoded: Lincoln Riley and his USC Trojans headed into the bye week with serious optimism after knocking off Penn State in front of over 114,000 Nittany Lion fans wearing white. On Saturday evening, however, a complete 180. The Trojans fell flat on their faces at Camp Randall Stadium, losing 24-7 to the Wisconsin Badgers. Chances of an appearance in the College Football Playoff are now close to none, with USC almost certainly needing to run the table through its final four games. Unfortunately for them, three of those matchups will come against Ohio State, Indiana and UCLA. "Just flat-out didn't play good enough on any of the three sides of the ball," Riley said after the loss. "Didn't coach good enough, made critical errors on the road...I take responsibility for it. It's hard to win on the road, and you have to play a lot better than we did tonight." It started with an offensive unit that had perhaps its worst display since Riley took over as head coach of the program. Their lowest point total since his arrival had been 17 before coming 10 short of that mark on Saturday. The Trojans had also not been held under 14 points in a game since 2018. Jayden Maiava threw the ball a season-high 50 times, completing 31 passes for a single touchdown and two interceptions. Both of his giveaways came in a nightmare first quarter for USC that smothered any sort of opportunity to get off to a fast start on the road. The Badgers pick off Jayden Maiava FOR A SECOND TIME! 📺 Big Ten Saturday Night on NBC & Peacock pic.twitter.com/GRHnMzoZUQ — NBC Sports (@NBCSports) October 25, 2026 "Flat out, I just didn't play great," Maiava said. "I got to play better for my teammates." When things weren't going right through the air, they were somehow going worse on the ground. The Trojans managed to carry the ball 25 times for a total of -17 rush yards. Maiava finished with -57 himself. Anthony Wahl-Imagn Images Through all the dismay, USC only found itself trailing 10-7 at halftime thanks to a four-yard touchdown grab from tight end Taniela Tupou in the second quarter. The full unraveling took place in the final 30 minutes of the contest. The Badgers only continued to expand upon their three-point advantage, which had initially been provided via a five-yard rushing touchdown late in the second quarter from former Trojan Bryan Jackson. Wisconsin quarterback Colton Joseph handed the ball off on six of 10 plays on the Badgers' opening drive of the half, capping it off with a 16-yard touchdown pass to Chris Brooks Jr. for the score. USC finished its next drive by seeing Caden Chittenden's 44-yard field goal attempt get blocked. Joseph led yet another scoring drive in the fourth quarter that chewed nearly eight minutes of clock, with Ryan Schwendeman's one-yard rushing touchdown helping the Badgers extend their lead to 24-7 with just 5:21 to go. On the drive beforehand, it was more disaster from the special teams unit for the Trojans, as Chittenden missed a 58-yard attempt that came up way short. His season-high for a made field goal had been just 39 yards. By the time the clock had ticked its way to the end of the fourth quarter, USC had taken the form of a team that was discouraged and defeated. They dropped to 6-2 on the season and 3-2 in the Big Ten. Wisconsin, meanwhile, earned its second victory against a ranked opponent and improved to 5-2. A tale of total opposites left the Trojans on the embarrassing end of a defeat that will once again have the fanbase calling for Riley's job. This time around, are the complaints genuinely justified? They very well might be. Wisconsin was simply relentless in the run game, putting the ball on the ground 42 times and accumulating 142 rushing yards. Joseph needed to throw the ball just 14 times and had only 58 passing yards. Maiava was sacked five times. USC was flagged for six penalties that totaled 51 yards, while Wisconsin committed just four for 30 yards. As Riley said, those are critical errors. You can't expect to win in front of 71,750 at Camp Randall if that's the product. The noise from critics will be at a new high for the 2026 season, but the Trojans need to pick themselves up off the mat quickly with No. 3 Ohio State coming to the Coliseum on Halloween night. Another performance like Saturday's against the Badgers, and things will get even scarier in Los Angeles. One possible beam of light for the Trojans: the Buckeyes will be without starting quarterback Julian Sayin, who is out indefinitely after injuring his shoulder on Oct. 17 at Indiana. Unfortunately, Jeremiah Smith still exists, and the Heisman frontrunner will be hungry to add another marquee performance to his ledger. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:30 p.m. PT.

item.title: Diving deeper into Cavs narrow 125-121 victory over the Nets
item.description: Oct 24, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Cleveland Cavaliers guard Donovan Mitchell (45) drives to the basket against Brooklyn Nets forward Chaney Johnson (31) during the second half at Rocket Arena. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect CLEVELAND — The Cleveland Cavaliers nearly fumbled a 22-point fourth-quarter lead as they defeated the Brooklyn Nets 125-121 in their home opener. Three stars of the game First star: Michael Porter Jr. 28 points, 9 rebounds, 1 assist, 4 steals Being an off-ball scoring threat on an otherwise inept offense is difficult. Ideally, Porter would be creating looks through his movement and receiving passes from someone that actually requires defensive attention — say, Nikola Jokic. Instead, Porter has to work off Egor Demin and Julius Randle, which isn’t always the easiest task. However, Porter made that look easy this game. He was disruptive off-ball, drawing the defense’s attention away from the play, and when he did get an opening, he made the most of it. This was on top of being an impactful defender. Second star: Jarrett Allen 21 points, 8 rebounds, 1 steal Allen was limited to 27 minutes, presumably because of the knee injury he is playing through , but made the most of his time on the court. He was aggressive attacking in the pick-and-roll when the Nets blitzed the ball handler, and even threw in a three-point make from the top of the arc. Aside from maybe the three-point attempt, this was exactly what you want to see from Allen. And the Cavs were once again better off because he was a meaningful part of the offensive attack. Third star: Donovan Mitchell 22 points, 4 assists, 5 rebounds, 1 steal Mitchell’s scoring is in midseason form. There are things you could criticize him for in these first two games— particularly the turnovers — but scoring isn’t one of them. The shotmaking has felt effortless at the start of the season. He’s doing a good job of creating space off the dribble, allowing him to score at all three levels. Interestingly enough, Mitchell isn’t hunting off-the-dribble threes as much as we’ve seen in the past. He’s only taken 10 triples through two games, with most of them being catch-and-shoot threes. The three-point volume is something to keep an eye on as the season progresses. Dud of the game Day’Ron Sharpe 7 points, 1 assist, 8 rebounds, 2 turnovers, 6 fouls This was a tough game for Sharpe. Defensively, he struggled to contain Allen and Evan Mobley — who had a good game in his own right — and fouled James Harden twice on three-point attempts. This all led to him fouling out midway through the fourth quarter. Offensively, he struggled to make much of an impact against Cleveland’s bigs. He went just 3-for-10 from the field while turning it over three times. Cavalier who deserves a shoutout Jaylon Tyson 15 points, 4 assists, 1 steal Tyson provided a solid contribution off the bench. He played with energy, knocked down some threes, and did a good job finding open
item.content:encoded: Oct 24, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Cleveland Cavaliers guard Donovan Mitchell (45) drives to the basket against Brooklyn Nets forward Chaney Johnson (31) during the second half at Rocket Arena. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect CLEVELAND — The Cleveland Cavaliers nearly fumbled a 22-point fourth-quarter lead as they defeated the Brooklyn Nets 125-121 in their home opener. Three stars of the game First star: Michael Porter Jr. 28 points, 9 rebounds, 1 assist, 4 steals Being an off-ball scoring threat on an otherwise inept offense is difficult. Ideally, Porter would be creating looks through his movement and receiving passes from someone that actually requires defensive attention — say, Nikola Jokic. Instead, Porter has to work off Egor Demin and Julius Randle, which isn’t always the easiest task. However, Porter made that look easy this game. He was disruptive off-ball, drawing the defense’s attention away from the play, and when he did get an opening, he made the most of it. This was on top of being an impactful defender. Second star: Jarrett Allen 21 points, 8 rebounds, 1 steal Allen was limited to 27 minutes, presumably because of the knee injury he is playing through , but made the most of his time on the court. He was aggressive attacking in the pick-and-roll when the Nets blitzed the ball handler, and even threw in a three-point make from the top of the arc. Aside from maybe the three-point attempt, this was exactly what you want to see from Allen. And the Cavs were once again better off because he was a meaningful part of the offensive attack. Third star: Donovan Mitchell 22 points, 4 assists, 5 rebounds, 1 steal Mitchell’s scoring is in midseason form. There are things you could criticize him for in these first two games— particularly the turnovers — but scoring isn’t one of them. The shotmaking has felt effortless at the start of the season. He’s doing a good job of creating space off the dribble, allowing him to score at all three levels. Interestingly enough, Mitchell isn’t hunting off-the-dribble threes as much as we’ve seen in the past. He’s only taken 10 triples through two games, with most of them being catch-and-shoot threes. The three-point volume is something to keep an eye on as the season progresses. Dud of the game Day’Ron Sharpe 7 points, 1 assist, 8 rebounds, 2 turnovers, 6 fouls This was a tough game for Sharpe. Defensively, he struggled to contain Allen and Evan Mobley — who had a good game in his own right — and fouled James Harden twice on three-point attempts. This all led to him fouling out midway through the fourth quarter. Offensively, he struggled to make much of an impact against Cleveland’s bigs. He went just 3-for-10 from the field while turning it over three times. Cavalier who deserves a shoutout Jaylon Tyson 15 points, 4 assists, 1 steal Tyson provided a solid contribution off the bench. He played with energy, knocked down some threes, and did a good job finding open teammates as a connector. This was basically an ideal game for him. Play of the game James Harden: DROPPIN' DIMES. This one to Jarrett Allen was around multiple defenders 😮 pic.twitter.com/OJ44yV05HG — NBA (@NBA) October 24, 2026 Assists like this show why Harden is one of the best passers in NBA history. Few guards would’ve seen this angle, let alone been able to fit the ball into such a tight window. This was a bright spot in what was an overall a poor showing from Harden. Quote of the day “This is a building block. It’s time spent. It’s adversity. I think Joe Mazzulla said something like everybody loves each other in training camp. But you understand, like hey, come December, come January, and we’re missing shots…who are we then? That all comes in the regular season.” – Donovan Mitchell on the early season struggles Stat of the game The Cavs have been outscored 73-45 combined in the fourth quarter through two games. Late game execution has left a lot to be desired. This game will be remembered for the Cavaliers not learning their lesson from Thursday The Cavs didn’t give up their 22-point fourth-quarter lead, but it didn’t stop them from trying. The Nets cut the deficit down to two by winning the fourth quarter in the closing minute before the Cavs iced the game at the free-throw line. Brooklyn won the final frame 41-29. The Cavaliers spent the time since Thursday’s loss to the Sixers talking about how they need to do a better job of handling leads . They didn’t do that here. If they were playing a team that was slightly more competent than the Nets, they likely would’ve dropped this one as well. The Cavs are clearly a work in progress. They’re incorporating new pieces into the rotation that will take some time. However, it’s impossible to feel great about what you’ve seen so far — particularly in their first two fourth quarters.

Spurs, who had won on one of their previous 34 trips to west London, were already 1-0 up when Palmer earned a second yellow card for catching Conor Gallagher with a late tackle. item.title: Why Stanley Matthews’ Ballon d’Or triumph echoes down the years for Harry Kane | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In 1956, the Blackpool great was recognised for his force of individual will, the very thing that makes the Bayern and England striker the standout candiate Systems football began In 1963 (On the hallowed turf at Wembley) With the impact of a cynical foul By Gino Pivatelli. At that moment in the European Cup final, when the hard-working Milan forward, brought in to combat Benfica’s Mário Coluna, caught the great playmaker, football of the individual came to an end. The foul not only checked a promising break, but broke a bone in Coluna’s foot. Without substitutes, he hobbled on, diminished, and Milan won 2-1 to lift the trophy and register the first victory for a team that prioritised the system over the individual. Modern football was born. Continue reading...

item.description: Hammers humbled at home; Swansea thrashed 5-0 Burnley sack manager Hayen after 4-1 loss at Lincoln Southampton announced themselves in the promotion race with a statement 3-2 win at the pre-season title favourites, West Ham . Kuryu Matsuki, James Bree and Lewis Dobbin were all on target in a chaotic first half, while Kyle Walker-Peters and Tomas Soucek replied for the Hammers. Nuno Espírito Santo’s side would have gone top with a win but instead saw their nine-match unbeaten run halted. There were thousands of empty seats by the end at the London Stadium, with those who stayed booing the Hammers off. Southampton, deducted four points at the start of the season, are now just two points behind West Ham. Continue reading...

item.title: Scottish Premiership: Kelsy fires Rangers to emphatic win; Dundee United pip Aberdeen
item.description: Rangers 4-0 St Johnstone; Dundee United 3-2 Aberdeen Kevin Kelsy scores two to sink 10-man Saints Derek McInnes asked his Rangers side to be “brilliant” against St Johnstone and was rewarded with a 4-0 Premiership win at Ibrox. After dropping two points at Dundee last Saturday , the Light Blues dominated the first half but only led at the interval through a goal in the 29th minute from the Venezuela forward Kevin Kelsy. Saints started the second half brightly but goals from the Gers striker Ryan Naderi in the 61st minute and Kelsy again five minutes later had the home side cruising. The Saints substitute Kai Fotheringham was shown a straight red card by Chris Graham in the 74th minute for his high challenge on the midfielder Nico Raskin, before the substitute Tochi Chukwuani added a fourth for the hosts with three minutes remaining. This story will be updated after Sunday’s matches Continue reading...

item.description: Defender costs three goals in past two league matches Emery praises ‘fantastic’ match-winner Jackson Enzo Maresca is not concerned by the form of Marc Guéhi despite the defender costing his side three goals in the past two Premier League matches, the Manchester City manager said after seeing his side lose in the league for the first time this season. Nicolas Jackson’s double earned Aston Villa a 2-1 victory at Villa Park after Guéhi was unable to control the ball for the opener. Instead he spilled it into the path of John McGinn, who played it to Jackson, allowing him to score the first of two goals. The defender was then substituted at half-time having been booked on 32 minutes. Guéhi’s errors allowed Ipswich to score twice against City last weekend. Continue reading...

item.title: Vincent Kompany to miss ‘weeks, not days’ with virus treatment, say Bayern Munich
item.description: Head coach in hospital after collapsing in training Assistant coach Aaron Danks to take charge against Freiburg Bayern Munich expect Vincent Kompany to miss an extended period as their head coach continues his hospital treatment for a virus after collapsing on the training pitch on Friday. Speaking at a press conference on Saturday, Bayern’s sporting director, Max Eberl, confirmed Kompany was still in hospital in a stable condition. Kompany’s English assistant coach, Aaron Danks, will replace the 40-year-old for Sunday’s Bundesliga match at Freiburg. Eberl said examinations were continuing to determine the nature of the former Manchester City and Belgium captain’s condition, with a recovery timeframe yet to be determined. Continue reading...

item.title: Older, calmer, but still playing the hits: Mourinho and Madrid primed for clásico
item.description: Once Bobby Robson’s translator at the Camp Nou, José Mourinho is tasked with bringing down Barcelona on Sunday José Mourinho has done the por que?, the printout and the press conference no-show, and he’s been here only three months. The Real Madrid manager has played the classics without even playing a clásico. Not yet anyway, but it’s time: on Sunday night he returns to the stadium he first arrived at 30 transformative years ago as Bobby Robson’s talented young translator, and last visited in 2013 as the most famous manager in football. The coach who once declared “today, tomorrow and always, Barcelona in my heart,” and claimed he would only ever go to Real Madrid to destroy them, has been entrusted with attempting to bring about the destruction of Barcelona. It is not the first time: if his return is about nostalgia, which it is, that’s wrapped up in their rivals too. Continue reading...

item.title: Arteta concerned over Saka’s durability as forward faces possible six-week absence
item.description: Arteta: ‘We need to understand how to manage his load’ Max Dowman could play against Everton on Saturday Mikel Arteta has expressed concern over Bukayo Saka’s robustness after a series of injuries to the forward in the past year and as he awaits further news on how long he will be out for with a thigh issue. Saka is set for an MRI scan after limping off in the 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League, with Arteta revealing the 25-year-old had “quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury”. Saka will definitely miss Saturday’s game against Evertonand, it is understood, Arsenal fear it could be a grade-two tear that could potentially keep him out for up to six weeks. Continue reading...

item.title: Enciso rescues point in storm for Ipswich to deny Nottingham Forest
item.description: Amid a Suffolk squall, winds whipping, a constant drum of rain, an encounter full of half-chances, mistakes, the obligatory refereeing controversy and searching questions. Do Ipswich possess the stones to deal with the big league? Perhaps so. How long can Nottingham Forest’s dip sustain before their president, Evangelos Marinakis, takes his usual course of action. Perhaps not much longer. Ipswich’s Gary O’Neil was the happier manager, Forest had created the cleaner opportunities, only for familiar failings to cost them. “We were never quite good enough with the ball to turn it into a football match,” said O’Neil. Further adding to Forest’s disappointment, Ipswich’s Issa Diop escaped what looked, on first glance, a red card for a last-man foul. A first-half exchange of goals, both owing much to defensive laxness, determined the result. Continue reading...

item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Mamdani loves Arsenal. He should challenge them to cut ties with the UAE over Sudan | Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. Continue reading...

item.title: Crystal Palace and Newcastle face off with both in search of season kickstart
item.description: Pierre Sage and Matthias Jaissle face some key questions: both were appointed this summer yet form, and results, have proved elusive Conceding 17 goals in seven Premier League matches is not exactly the start Pierre Sage or Crystal Palace’s hierarchy would have hoped for. The transition from Oliver Glasner’s counterattacking 3-4-2-1 formation to the Frenchman’s more aggressive approach has exposed massive weaknesses in defence, culminating with last week’s humiliating defeat at Brighton. Palace fans became used to success under Glasner and they are already looking nervously over their shoulders at the bottom three. Even their league wins under Sage so far – against Fulham and Nottingham Forest – could have ended in defeat. Something doesn’t seem right in south London. EA Continue reading...

item.title: Pascal Gross: the obsessive runner keeping Brighton ‘one step ahead’ after fast start
item.description: Midfielder ‘who can never stand still’ has brought renewed energy to Seagulls since return to the club in January Most footballers like to spend their summers unwinding after a long season but not Pascal Gross. Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 , the midfielder entered – and won – a running race. Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor. Continue reading...

item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...
